The main drawback of missed payments is the waiting period described above.
7-9.note: The 2025 Notice No. 22 from the National Healthcare Security Administration does not appear on the Administration’s official website or on the Chinese Government website. Figures of 700 yuan and 400 yuan match documents from Hebei and Anhui provinces; the Anhui document explicitly cites the same notice. While receiving unemployment benefits, an individual’s employee‑based medical insurance is paid for by the unemployment fund, so there is no need to enroll separately.

7-10.t: For serious illnesses, use yibao, dibao, medical assistance, and cross‑regional registration first — avoid online loans
7-10.cost: There is no direct expense. The steps must be followed in order. First, before being hospitalized in another province, register via the “National Medical Insurance Administration” WeChat official account using the “National Cross‑Regional Medical Registration” mini‑program. Second, settle the bill directly upon discharge. Third, if the remaining amount after reimbursement is still unaffordable, apply to the local township government or subdistrict office for medical assistance. Fourth, if you are still employed, take sick leave for the duration of your medical period — the time during which you cannot be dismissed despite being unable to work due to illness; workers injured on the job should use workers’ compensation instead. Fifth, if you cannot repay credit‑card debt, proactively negotiate a repayment plan with the bank. Sixth, as a last resort, use a personal fundraising platform authorized by the civil affairs bureau to raise money. The main documents required are a diagnosis certificate, itemized cost list, and settlement statement; you’ll need to make two to four trips. The difficulty lies in having to handle all these procedures while you are ill.
7-10.human: The sequence is fixed. Before any cross‑regional hospitalization, register through the “National Medical Insurance Administration” WeChat account; settlement occurs automatically at discharge, so you need not pay the full amount upfront. If the post‑reimbursement cost remains high, apply for medical assistance at the township or subdistrict level. Employed individuals are entitled to a medical leave period ranging from three to 24 months, during which they cannot be fired. Steer clear of online loans and high‑interest private borrowing.
7-10.gain: The state bundles basic medical insurance, dibao, and medical assistance into what is known as the “triple safety net,” providing layered protection. Eligible recipients on dibao or in extreme poverty receive at least 70 % coverage for qualifying medical expenses. Even those who are not impoverished but become financially strained by illness may apply for additional aid. Proper pre‑registration enables direct hospital billing without upfront cash payments. The medical leave period — three to 24 months depending on length of service — guarantees job security; sick‑leave pay must be no less than 80 % of the local minimum wage. Injured workers enjoy a “work‑rest period” during which full wages and benefits are preserved, typically for up to 12 months. Credit‑card debtors who negotiate a customized repayment schedule with their bank can spread payments over a maximum of five years, and the bank must cease collection efforts thereafter. Only platforms officially designated by the civil affairs bureau may be used for personal fundraising; they must verify authenticity and disburse donations solely to the applicant.
7-10.note: The exact percentage of reimbursement and annual limits under medical assistance are set locally. Medical leave is divided into six tiers based on total work experience and tenure at the current employer; exceeding this period may permit lawful termination, so it is wise to know your tier. Emergency cases also require registration; however, the official website does not clarify whether such cases are automatically registered or can be added later — contact your local insurer for clarification. Avoid online loans and high‑interest private borrowing; courts only protect debt up to four times the one‑year LPR (see item 15). Any amount above that remains legally payable, though pursuing legal action while ill is impractical. Critical emergencies demand immediate 120 ambulance service; hospitals must provide care without delay or cost barriers, with expenses covered by the emergency medical assistance fund (see section 24, item 8). The original text of Ministry of Labor Decree No. 309 (1995) is unavailable on the Ministry’s site; the cited provisions are reproduced from a provincial labor authority.

7-11.t: Replace a lost ID card immediately; get a temporary one if you need it urgently
7-11.cost: There is a fee for issuing the ID card. This is a legally mandated charge set by the state; the exact amount is posted locally. You must apply at the police station in your area of permanent residence — just one visit is required.
7-11.human: For standard replacements, the new ID card is issued within 60 days of submitting the application. If you need it right away, you can also request a temporary ID card on the spot; it is issued within 3 days and is valid for 3 months. Without an ID card, you cannot apply for jobs, rent accommodation, open bank accounts, or claim benefits — it is a prerequisite for all such procedures.
7-11.gain: Once you submit the application form for a resident ID card, authorities must issue the card within 60 days. During this period, if you urgently need identification, you may apply for a temporary resident ID card, which is issued within 3 days and remains valid for 3 months nationwide.
7-11.note: Without an ID card, it is impossible to secure employment, rent housing, open bank accounts, or receive benefits — it is a mandatory prerequisite for all such actions. The ID Card Law was amended in 2011; the text cited here is the version published in 2003, and current provisions apply. Whether applications can be submitted outside your home region depends on local police regulations.

7-12.t: After registering as unemployed, seek recognition as a person facing employment difficulties to receive social insurance subsidies or access to public welfare jobs
7-12.cost: There is no cost involved. You simply apply for recognition at a local public employment service center in your neighborhood or community. Eligibility criteria vary by region, but typically include being of advanced age, unemployed for a long time, a member of a dibao-receiving household, disabled, or part of a zero-employment household. First, you must complete unemployment registration before applying. The main difficulty lies in verifying whether you meet each individual criterion, and you must pay social insurance premiums upfront.
7-12.human: Once recognized, you can receive subsidies for your own social insurance payments — these generally cover up to two-thirds of the actual amount paid, for a maximum period of three years. If you are hired by an employer or placed in a public welfare job, the employer also qualifies for subsidies covering its share of social insurance contributions. Wages for public welfare jobs are set at or near the local minimum wage level. These jobs pay modest salaries but include social insurance benefits, making them a good transitional option. Keep in mind that most social insurance subsidies are paid retroactively, so you must pay the premiums first.
7-12.gain: After receiving this recognition, individuals who are not employed and pay their own social insurance premiums — known as flexible workers — become eligible for subsidies. These subsidies generally cover up to two-thirds of actual payments, for a maximum duration of three years. Employers hiring such individuals or placing them in public welfare jobs also receive subsidies covering their contributions toward pension, medical, and unemployment insurance. Public welfare jobs are positions created and funded by the government, with priority given to people facing employment difficulties. Additionally, one-time job-seeking subsidies are available for recent college graduates from dibao-receiving households, zero-employment households, or extremely poor families; disabled graduates and those who have taken national student loans also qualify. These subsidies are disbursed during the academic year following graduation (national framework; specific eligibility criteria and amounts are determined locally).
7-12.note: Public welfare jobs offer modest wages but include valuable social insurance benefits, making them ideal for a transition period. Most social insurance subsidies are paid after the fact, requiring upfront payment of premiums. For detailed eligibility requirements, contact 12333 or your local neighborhood office.

7-13.t: Apply for vocational training subsidies, employment internship subsidies, and social insurance subsidies during unemployment — don’t pay for training courses out of pocket
7-13.cost: There is no direct cost. However, training takes up a lot of your time. The real challenge is completing all required classes and earning the necessary certificates before you can receive any subsidies.
7-13.human: You won’t have to pay for training yourself. If you complete approved training and earn the required certificates, you can qualify for vocational training subsidies — up to three times per person. Recent college graduates who haven’t found jobs within two years, as well as unemployed youth aged 16–24, can join employment internships and receive basic living allowances during that time. First, check the “Vocational Training Subsidy Directory” on your local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau website — don’t sign up for paid courses on your own.
7-13.gain: Regulations issued by the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security outline several employment assistance programs funded specifically to support job seekers. Eligible individuals can receive vocational training subsidies up to three times per person after completing approved training and earning the required certificates. Those facing employment difficulties who pay for their own social insurance (as self-employed workers) can get subsidies for up to three years; this period extends until retirement for anyone within five years of reaching the statutory retirement age. Recent college graduates can receive similar social insurance subsidies for up to two years, while those hired by employers qualify for up to one year of support. Additionally, recent graduates without jobs and unemployed youth aged 16–24 can join employment internships and receive basic living allowances during that period.
7-13.note: Exact subsidy amounts and eligible programs vary by province; always check the “Vocational Training Subsidy Directory” on your local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau website. Extra one-time job-seeking and entrepreneurship subsidies are available for recent graduates from dibao families or zero-employment households, those with outstanding student loans, and individuals with disabilities.

7-14.t: Job hunting isn’t just about sending resumes — use a systematic approach: learn skills, set goals, and ask for help
7-14.cost: There’s no monetary cost. You’ll need to spend 1–2 hours each day for several weeks. Paid courses aren’t necessary; free career guidance from public employment services works just as well. The real challenge is staying consistent day after day without anyone watching over you, and actually reaching out to ask for help.
7-14.human: People who take part in job-hunting coaching are 2.67 times more likely to land a job than those who don’t. The most effective steps are: learning concrete job-hunting skills, clearly presenting yourself, setting clear goals, taking initiative, and asking for help. Turning this help into real results means getting referrals from people you know.
7-14.gain: A combined analysis of 47 peer-reviewed job-hunting coaching studies, all of which used experimental or quasi-experimental designs with control groups, shows that participants in coaching programs are 2.67 times more likely to find work than non-participants (OR 2.67, meaning a 2.67-fold increase in odds). The key components of effective coaching are: teaching job-hunting skills, improving self-presentation, boosting self-efficacy, encouraging proactive behavior, setting clear goals, and fostering social support through asking for help. Programs that combine skill training with motivation-building tactics deliver the best results.
7-14.note: Most of these studies were conducted in Europe and North America, and used structured group-based coaching programs. The findings here are extrapolations from those results, not data collected in China itself. Asking for social support means reaching out to acquaintances for introductions and referrals — so don’t hesitate to ask for their help.

7-15.t: No deposits, no ID retention, no “training loans”, no pyramid schemes, no usury
7-15.cost: Zero expense. If an employer or agency suggests “pay first, then get a job”, “pay for training before placement”, or “recruit others to earn money”, refuse immediately. Keep all chat logs and proof of any payments. The difficulty lies in the fact that when money is scarce, people may be tempted to take risks — saying “no” on the spot is not easy.
7-15.human: Employers cannot keep your ID or demand a deposit, nor can they charge you under any other pretext. If a job placement agency fails to find you a job, it must refund the placement fee. “Training loans” that require upfront fees, as well as pyramid schemes that pay out based on recruitment, are all officially recognized scams. Any interest on a loan exceeding four times the one-year LPR is not legally enforceable by courts, though the principal amount must still be repaid.
7-15.gain: Employers are prohibited from withholding IDs or demanding guarantees or deposits. Violations result in mandatory refunds and fines ranging from 500 to 2,000 RMB per worker. Job placement agencies likewise cannot retain IDs or collect deposits; if they fail to place you, they must return all fees. Schemes that demand training fees or loans under the guise of employment are flagged by multiple government agencies as “training loan” scams. Pyramid schemes, where earnings depend on recruiting others, are illegal; participants face fines up to 2,000 RMB. Interest on private loans exceeding four times the one-year LPR is not legally binding. This regulation replaced the previous tiered limits of 24% and 36% (nationwide, effective August 2020).
7-15.note: The four-times-LPR threshold represents the maximum legally protected interest rate; it does not mean the principal can be forgiven. This judicial interpretation was revised in December 2020, so current article numbers may differ from earlier versions. For guidance on converting installment and online loan fees into annualized rates, see Section 5, Article 7. Financial desperation makes individuals especially vulnerable to these schemes; instead, rely on legitimate resources such as unemployment benefits, labor dispute mediation, legal aid, shelters, or emergency assistance outlined earlier in this section.

7-16.t: Public rental housing for those with housing difficulties
7-16.cost: There is no fee to apply. You must submit documents to the local housing authority and provide written consent for them to verify the information you provide. If any documents are missing, they will inform you of what needs to be added at once. The waiting period for housing assignment is known as the “waiting queue period,” which generally does not exceed 5 years.
7-16.human: To qualify, you must meet three criteria simultaneously: you must have no property in the area, or your living space must fall below the required standard; your income and assets must also be below the set limits; and migrant workers must have maintained stable employment in the area for a specified period. The exact waiting queue period is announced locally. While this option cannot provide immediate relief, signing up costs nothing, and earlier applicants are more likely to be placed in housing sooner.
7-16.gain: Meeting all three conditions qualifies you to apply. First, you must have no property locally, or your living area must be smaller than the required minimum. Second, your income and assets must stay below the prescribed limits. Third, migrant workers must have held steady employment in the area for the mandated duration. Specific eligibility criteria are determined and released by housing authorities in municipalities and counties. Those who register for the queue are referred to as “waiting queue candidates,” and housing authorities are required to assign them a unit within the waiting queue period. (National framework; local areas set individual thresholds and rental rates; implemented since 2012.)
7-16.note: While this option cannot provide immediate relief, signing up costs nothing, and earlier applicants are more likely to be placed in housing sooner. Various other forms of subsidized housing exist locally, each with its own rules; please consult your local housing authority’s website for details.

7-17.t: Keep food and housing costs as low as possible: opt for monthly shared housing instead of daily rentals, and cook at home or use senior meal services rather than ordering takeout
7-17.cost: Finding a place to live takes 1–3 days. The security deposit is usually equal to one month’s rent (a rough estimate by the author). Cooking at home requires 30–60 minutes each day. The real challenge is staying disciplined enough to cook daily rather than ordering takeout.
7-17.human: In 2025, food accounted for 29.3% and housing for 21.7% of average national per‑capita spending — together they make up over half of all expenses. Therefore, cutting costs in these two areas yields the biggest savings. Based on the author’s experience, daily rentals and hourly rooms end up costing far more per month than shared housing; cooking at home is also cheaper than ordering takeout. When job hunting, ask whether housing and meals are provided — such offers effectively eliminate both major expense categories.
7-17.gain: In 2025, the average national per‑capita annual expenditure was 29,476 yuan. Of that amount, 8,631 yuan went toward food and alcohol, representing 29.3%. Housing costs totaled 6,397 yuan, or 21.7%. Together they constitute more than half of total spending, confirming that reducing these expenses delivers the greatest financial benefit. Senior meal services are now available to all older adults; they include senior cafeterias, dining tables, and meal assistance points, with additional subsidies for those in need. For context, as of 1 January 2026, the lowest first‑tier monthly minimum wage across all provinces was 2,080 yuan in Qinghai, while the highest was 2,740 yuan in Shanghai (national figures for 2025–2026).
7-17.note: Monthly costs for daily rentals and hourly rooms are considerably higher than those of shared housing; this is based on practical experience rather than official statistics. Rules regarding access to senior meal points for non‑seniors and their pricing vary by region. When seeking employment, be sure to ask whether housing and meals are included — such arrangements can completely eliminate these two major expense categories. The original Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security page could not be accessed; the figures cited here are taken from a republished page on the Sichuan Provincial Department of Human Resources and Social Security.

7-18.t: Don’t panic if your social insurance lapses: pension is calculated cumulatively, medical insurance is replenished per rules
7-18.cost: It costs nothing. Residents can pay for pension and medical insurance on an annual basis by themselves. If your employer‑based social insurance is interrupted, there’s no need to spend money on third‑party services to keep the coverage active just to avoid a “gap.”
7-18.human: Pension benefits are based on total years of contribution, not consecutive years. A break in payments doesn’t reset the count; once you’ve accumulated at least 15 years by retirement age, you can receive monthly payments. For employer‑based medical insurance, once you’ve met the required contribution period, you won’t need to pay further after retirement — though exact thresholds vary by region; call 12393 for local details. What really gets affected are eligibility criteria such as home purchase, household registration, or points accumulation, which often demand continuous coverage.
7-18.gain: Basic pension benefits are computed using total contribution years; interruptions don’t erase prior payments. Upon reaching retirement age, anyone with at least 15 years of contributions qualifies for monthly pension payouts. Those short of this threshold can keep contributing until they meet it. If you switch jobs across different administrative regions, your pension record transfers with you and continues to accrue. For employer‑based medical insurance, once cumulative contributions satisfy national minimums, no further payments are required after retirement. For residents, a lapse in medical insurance introduces a waiting period: after resuming payments, there’s a set interval during which medical expenses won’t be reimbursed (see Section 9 for details; nationwide rule).
7-18.note: The “national minimum years” requirement for exemption from post‑retirement employer‑based medical insurance varies by location and sometimes by gender; verify specifics via 12393 or your local medical insurance bureau. Gaps in coverage primarily impact eligibility for local programs demanding continuous contributions — such as home purchase, household registration, or points accumulation — each governed by regional policies. Paying third parties to maintain coverage artificially may result in financial loss or legal complications; this practice is not advised. For guidance on transferring pension and medical records when relocating, or on avoiding premature termination of coverage, refer to Section 19, Item 19 (Transferring pension and medical insurance records). Starting in 2030, the 15‑year threshold will increase by six months each year until it reaches 20 years; self‑employed individuals can calculate their own obligations using Section 5, Item 46 (Self‑employment pension contributions).

7-19.t: Even those who have served time, gone bankrupt, or ended up on a blacklist still have legal avenues to start anew — provided they complete the required procedures
7-19.cost: There are no application fees. Former inmates must register at their local judicial office or community center to apply for reintegration assistance and support from the government. Those on a defaulted-payer list must settle all debts before requesting removal from the list via the relevant court. In Shenzhen, individuals who have contributed to social insurance for at least three years may file for personal bankruptcy. Each step involves preparing documents, attending interviews, and undergoing a monitoring period of one to three years. The main difficulty lies in repeatedly recounting one’s past and enduring the lengthy observation phase.
7-19.human: Former inmates cannot be discriminated against regarding employment, education, or access to social insurance; those in financial hardship receive government aid. Minors under 18 at the time of their offense who received sentences of five years or less have their records sealed, so they need not disclose them when enlisting or seeking work. The blacklist remains active for two years; once debts are fully repaid, courts must remove the individual’s name within three working days. Adult criminal records are not sealed and must be disclosed when enlisting or applying for jobs.
7-19.gain: Former inmates are entitled to equal rights under the law and must not face discrimination in employment, education, or social insurance benefits. Those in need receive government assistance and support (as stipulated by the revised Prison Law effective 1 November 2026). Central directives from 2010 call for enhanced vocational training and inclusion in the dibao program for eligible individuals, alongside establishment of transitional reintegration centers. Minors under 18 with sentences under five years have sealed records; a certificate of no criminal record is issued within three working days upon request. The blacklist remains active for two years; removal occurs within three working days once debts are cleared. Shenzhen’s Personal Bankruptcy Regulations provide a unique legal pathway: after a three-year monitoring period, remaining debts may be discharged. Corporate entities facing insolvency may pursue restructuring, settlement, or liquidation, thereby extinguishing associated obligations (applicable nationwide; personal bankruptcy is currently limited to Shenzhen).
7-19.note: Adult criminal records are not sealed. Article 100 of the Criminal Law mandates disclosure of any prior convictions when enlisting or seeking employment. Certain professions — including civil servants, judges, lawyers, and teachers — face additional legal restrictions. Earlier provisions of the Prison Law (pre‑1 November 2026) correspond to Articles 37 and 38; exact wording depends on the effective version. Central Document No. 5 [2010] is referenced here via a regional government re‑publication, as the original text is unavailable on central portals. During the bankruptcy monitoring period, individuals may not travel first class, engage in excessive spending, or purchase property. Eight categories of debt — including compensation for intentional personal injury — remain non‑dischargeable; fraudulent claims may also be revoked. Removal from the blacklist does not automatically clear one’s credit history, as these are separate registries.

7-20.t: Before facing a serious illness, consider adding a one-year medical or critical illness insurance plan on top of basic medical insurance — just make sure to look for the phrase “guaranteed renewal.”
7-20.cost: For young people, a one-year expense-reimbursement medical plan costs only a few hundred yuan per year. This type of plan reimburses you based on actual medical expenses incurred. A critical illness policy, on the other hand, typically starts at several thousand yuan annually (these figures are rough estimates by the author; no official statistics are available). Purchasing such policies requires you to honestly disclose your health status — a process that takes about half an hour.
7-20.human: These insurance plans help cover the portion of medical costs and lost income that basic medical insurance does not. When shopping for a policy, be sure to check whether it explicitly states “guaranteed renewal.” Plans lacking this wording might be discontinued or have their premiums raised the following year. Honesty about your health history is mandatory; any concealment can lead to a denial of claims. First, make sure you’re enrolled in basic medical insurance before considering this option.
7-20.gain: Regulatory authorities classify such products into two main categories. Medical insurance reimburses you for actual medical expenses incurred, while critical illness insurance pays a predetermined lump sum upon diagnosis of specified illnesses. Both types are designed to cover out-of-pocket costs and lost earnings after basic medical insurance has been applied. Plans with a term of one year or less and no guaranteed renewal clause fall under short-term health insurance. Those with terms exceeding one year or that do include guaranteed renewal provisions are classified as long-term health insurance. “Guaranteed renewal” means that at the end of the term, the insurer must renew the policy under the same terms and at the same premium rate. Insurers are prohibited from encouraging the same individual to purchase multiple expense-reimbursement medical plans with overlapping coverage. Even if you buy two such plans, you can only receive reimbursement for the same expense once. The definitions of critical illnesses are standardized across the industry, covering 28 severe conditions and three milder ones. Malignant tumors, acute myocardial infarction, and sequelae of stroke are among the core conditions covered nationwide since 2019–2020.
7-20.note: This product is rated B because regulatory authorities provide only definitions and rules, without any concrete figures indicating how much money one can save by purchasing it. “Million-dollar medical insurance” is a marketing term; legally, it is considered short-term health insurance. Plans lacking a “guaranteed renewal” clause may be withdrawn or have their premiums increased the following year — so always verify this phrase in the policy wording. You cannot claim reimbursement twice for the same expense under two separate medical plans; avoid buying multiple such policies. Individuals with pre-existing conditions who fail to disclose them honestly risk having their claims denied. There is a two-year window after policy issuance during which insurers cannot terminate the contract or refuse claims solely on the grounds of nondisclosure; after this period, such grounds become valid. If fraud is detected within those two years, claims will be denied and premiums forfeited. For guidance on which types of losses are worth insuring against, see Section 5, Item 39 (“Losses you cannot afford to bear”). First, make sure you’re enrolled in basic resident medical insurance (see Item 9) before considering this option. The standardized definitions of critical illnesses were issued by industry associations under the guidance of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission, rather than by government decree.

7-21.t: When there’s nowhere else to sleep, 24‑hour venues can only serve as a temporary overnight refuge; shelters should be the first choice
7-21.cost: Waiting areas at airports and train stations are usually free. Fast‑food restaurants and internet cafés require some spending. Sleep is often restless, and there’s a risk of theft. The real difficulty is staying awake all night.
7-21.human: Airports and train stations can provide a place to spend the night — they have restrooms and power outlets — but no official data confirms they’re safe. Shelters employ staff around the clock; anyone arriving at night receives immediate assistance. In winter, some regions even open temporary cold‑weather shelters. Those unwilling to enter a shelter still get food, warm clothing, and other necessities from patrol officers.
7-21.gain: 24‑hour venues allow a person to survive the night with access to restrooms and charging points, though no official figures exist on their safety. Under Civil Affairs Bureau regulations, helplines must remain open 24/7, and shelters must provide round‑the‑clock care. Individuals without stable housing, victims of theft or robbery, or those suddenly left without income may qualify for emergency transitional support. In certain areas, community centers also serve as temporary shelters, especially in winter. Patrols increase during nighttime, cold spells, rain, snow, or ice; key locations include train stations, docks, underpasses, bridges, and construction sites (since 2013, Civil Affairs Bureaus nationwide run annual winter outreach programs).
7-21.note: Safety risks are real. Keep valuables close, avoid accepting drinks or food from strangers, and steer clear of isolated corners. Never sleep under bridges, along rivers, or at construction sites at night; extreme weather can be fatal. Details on meals, lodging, and travel vouchers at shelters are covered in Section 4 (“Turning to a shelter when all else fails”). Shelters only assist individuals unable to secure basic needs on their own and lacking supportive relatives or friends. Applicants must give honest information; those who refuse to cooperate receive no aid. The Civil Affairs Bureau directive referenced here dates to winter 2022; yearly updates apply locally. Some venues conduct midnight clear‑outs — avoid confrontations with security personnel.

7-22.t: If you’re owed wages, first figure out who hired you: unlicensed workshops and subcontractors can still be reported to labor authorities; only work done for private households falls under civil court jurisdiction
7-22.cost: No cost involved. First, determine three things: whether the employer runs a business, whether the work was subcontracted from a company or construction site, and whether you were hired by a private household. You can check whether a business holds a license via the national enterprise credit registry.
7-22.human: Unlicensed workshops and shops that owe wages can still be reported to labor authorities and face labor arbitration; their owners can also be held personally liable. If a subcontractor fails to pay wages, the main contractor or construction entity is responsible for payment. Only work performed for private households — such as domestic help — does not qualify as a labor dispute and must be resolved in civil court.
7-22.gain: Article 2 of the Labor Contract Law defines “employers” as enterprises, individual economic organizations, private non-enterprise units, and similar entities; private individuals are excluded. Supreme Court interpretations specify several scenarios that do not constitute labor disputes: conflicts between households or individuals and domestic workers; disputes between independent craftsmen and their helpers or apprentices; and disputes between rural contract farmers and their employees. These cases must be filed in civil court under standard civil procedures, with a three-year statute of limitations. Unlicensed employers do not fall under these exceptions. Article 93 of the Labor Contract Law states that employers lacking valid operating licenses must pay workers for any labor rendered, plus compensation and damages. Article 29 of the same interpretation mandates that unlicensed employers or their owners be named as parties in any dispute. The Labor Security Supervision Regulations, Article 33, authorizes labor authorities to investigate unlicensed entities engaging in labor activities. Under Article 94, both the contracting organization and the unlicensed operator bear joint liability for any harm caused to workers. Finally, Article 36 of the Regulations on Guaranteeing Migrant Workers’ Wages requires main contractors or construction firms to settle any wage arrears incurred by unlicensed subcontractors or individuals (nationwide).
7-22.note: Follow this sequence when assessing your case. First, determine whether the work was subcontracted from a company or construction site; if so, approach the main contractor or general builder. Per Section 2, wage-specific accounts and general contractors are obligated to make upfront payments. Next, verify whether the employer operates a business; licensed or not, such entities can be reported to labor authorities and subjected to arbitration, with owners named as respondents. Only when work is performed for private households should you pursue civil court action. Keep in mind that filing a lawsuit requires you to initiate proceedings and provide evidence; standard civil trials take at least six months. Legal fees are not recoverable from the losing party, so you must bear them yourself unless eligible for legal aid per Section 3. If you possess a written debt acknowledgment, you may apply for a payment order; smaller claims can be handled via small claims court as outlined in Section 8, Article 22. The three-year statute of limitations applies, as detailed in Section 8, Article 19. No legal pathway guarantees repayment; even if successful, you may receive nothing if the employer lacks assets.

8-1.t: After a traffic accident, stop, help the injured, and call the police — don’t flee
8-1.cost: No cost at all. Stopping, turning on hazard lights, helping the injured, and calling the police will take at most one or two hours. In minor accidents where no one is hurt and both parties agree on what happened, you can first take photos, then note down the other driver’s name, phone number, license plate, driver’s license number, insurance policy number, and the damaged parts of the vehicles. After both parties sign a statement, they may leave the scene and later negotiate a settlement.
8-1.human: If you flee the scene, you are automatically considered fully responsible for the accident. Your driver’s license will be revoked, and you won’t be allowed to retake the test for life. More practically, both collision damage coverage and third‑party liability insurance will not pay any claims related to fleeing — you’d have to cover hundreds of thousands of dollars out of pocket. Staying on the scene to help and call the police only takes a couple of hours.
8-1.gain: The person who flees bears full responsibility for the accident. Only if you can prove the other driver also acted negligently might that responsibility be reduced. Fleeing also results in license revocation for life. If the incident meets the criteria for a traffic‑related crime, fleeing can lead to a sentence of 3 to 7 years; if someone dies because of it, the sentence rises to more than 7 years. Insurance won’t help either: both collision damage coverage and third‑party liability policies exclude any claims arising from “hit‑and‑run,” “intentional tampering with or falsifying the scene,” or “destruction of evidence,” leaving you responsible for any compensation costs (nationwide).
8-1.note: If anyone is injured, first provide aid and then call the police. If moving vehicles or people is necessary to help, mark their original positions first. Even if you feel no impact after a minor collision and drive away, that can still be classified as fleeing — when in doubt, call the police. The insurance information cited comes from standard industry clauses; the actual coverage you receive depends on the specific terms of your own policy.

8-2.t: If you realize you’ve been scammed, call 110 or 96110 right away to request a stop‑payment — don’t try to investigate on your own first
8-2.cost: No cost at all. Just make one call, clearly stating the time of the transfer, the amount, and the scammer’s account number. Keep screenshots of the transfer and any chat records.
8-2.human: The brief period right after money is sent is the only window of opportunity. During this time police can issue an emergency stop‑payment order and quickly freeze the funds; banks are required to comply. Once the money has been moved through multiple accounts and scattered, it becomes almost impossible to recover. Therefore, call 110 or 96110 immediately — don’t waste time investigating or asking questions on your own. Calls to 96110 come from police officers trying to warn you, so be sure to answer them.
8-2.gain: Law enforcement has the authority to instantly query, urgently stop‑pay, and swiftly freeze any funds linked to a scam. Banks and payment services must cooperate. Once frozen, those funds are returned to victims according to established procedures. The sooner a stop‑payment is ordered, the higher the chance of recovery; after the money has been dispersed, success rates drop dramatically. 96110 is the nationwide anti‑fraud hotline; calls from this number are police warnings, so you must answer them. (Nationwide, effective December 2022)
8-2.note: Anyone claiming to be from police, prosecutors, or courts and asking you to transfer money to a “secure account” is running a scam. The law merely mandates the creation of a stop‑payment and freezing mechanism so banks can hold the funds. How much can be recovered depends on whether the money is still in the account at the time you report it. Information about the “National Anti‑Fraud Center” app and 96110 is taken from a Fujian Provincial Public Security Department page; the original page on the Ministry of Public Security’s site cannot be accessed.

8-3.t: Remember the core anti-fraud rules: don’t trust unsolicited calls, don’t share personal information, don’t click on suspicious links, and always verify any transfer requests. All seven of the most common scam types follow this same pattern
8-3.cost: No cost at all. Just memorize the “three no’s and one extra check” rule, read through the descriptions of the seven scam types below, and install the “National Anti-Fraud Center” app. Make sure to answer any calls from 96110. If someone asks you to transfer money, share your screen, download an unknown app, click a link, or share verification codes, hang up first and then call the official hotline to verify. The hard part is that scammers often pressure you to act immediately — you must resist that pressure and hang up first.
8-3.human: If someone asks you to transfer money, share your screen, download an unknown app, click a link, or share verification codes, hang up first and then call the official number to verify. The seven most common scam types are fake “task reward” schemes, fraudulent investment offers, fake loan scams, impersonation of customer service agents, impersonation of police or judicial officials, romance scams, and fake “task reward” schemes involving seduction. All of them aim to get you to send money first. Spotting them in advance is far cheaper than trying to recover lost funds later.
8-3.gain: By law, government agencies and relevant departments must inform the public about common tactics used in telecom and online fraud. Public security authorities, together with financial, telecom, and internet regulators, run a nationwide early warning and prevention system to reach out to people at risk of being scammed. 96110 is this unified national hotline for such warnings — you should always answer calls from it. According to a June 2026 report from the Ministry of Public Security, the top 10 most common scam types account for 85% of all telecom fraud cases. Fake “task reward” schemes are the most prevalent, making up 25% of all cases. Fraudulent investment offers cause the greatest financial losses, accounting for roughly 40% of total fraud-related losses. The Fujian Provincial Public Security Department has outlined specific identifying features for each type. For fake “task reward” schemes: “Anyone urging you to join a money-making scheme is likely trying to take your money; they won’t refund your initial deposit unless you complete endless tasks.” For fraudulent investment offers: “Fake promoters post fake profit reports in online groups; they give small initial returns to encourage you to invest more, then demand ‘taxes’ before allowing any withdrawals.” For fake loan scams: “Legitimate loans never require upfront deposits or proof of bank transactions; any such requests are a red flag.” For impersonation of customer service agents: “They claim you have an active membership that will incur automatic fees and harm your credit score, pressuring you to transfer money to cancel it.” For impersonation of police or judicial officials: “No legitimate police or judicial agency has any so-called ‘safe accounts’; any ‘law enforcement’ contact via phone, QQ, WeChat, or online platforms is a scam.” For romance scams: “Never trust anyone you’ve only met via photos or video calls; they often invent urgent reasons to ask for money without ever agreeing to a video chat or in-person meeting.” For seduction-based “task reward” schemes: “They arrange a meeting first, then demand you complete ‘tasks’ that require ever-larger payments.” Spotting these scams early is far cheaper than trying to reverse unauthorized transfers later. How much money you can recover depends on whether it remains in your account at the time of reporting; for details on how to request a transfer reversal, see section 2 (call 110 or 96110 to request a reversal). (Nationwide, effective December 2022)
8-3.note: Scammers posing as police, judicial officials, customer service agents, supervisors, or platform risk control staff all use the same basic tactic: they ask you to “cooperate with an investigation”, “cancel a membership”, “join a task reward scheme”, or “access insider investment opportunities”. Legitimate loans never require upfront deposits, and no police or judicial agency has any “safe accounts” — remembering these two facts alone can help you avoid most scams. This is graded B because the “three no’s and one extra check” rule is only an official public awareness slogan; there are no hard statistics showing exactly how much it reduces scam victimization. The rule and the list of seven scam types are taken from provincial public security department websites. The top 10 scam types identified by the Ministry of Public Security in 2026 also include impersonation of e-commerce and logistics customer service agents, fake loan and credit report scams, fraudulent online gaming transactions, fake online dating schemes, impersonation of supervisors or acquaintances, and fake flight cancellation/refund offers — all of them follow the same pattern of ultimately demanding a money transfer. If an acquaintance asks you in person to “help with a face scan” for a loan — no transfer, but you end up as the borrower — see item 45 (help with a face scan). Store-operation scams when doing business are in Section 12, item 24 (store operations and opening-store training).

8-4.t: Seeing a face on video or hearing a voice on the phone does not count as verification; if a transfer is involved, hang up first and call back using an old number saved in your contacts
8-4.cost: No cost involved. It only requires making one extra call and waiting a few extra minutes. In general, avoid posting videos of your face or long voice recordings on public accounts. The hard part is that scammers often pressure you to act quickly — you must resist the urge to transfer money right away.
8-4.human: Seeing someone’s face or hearing their voice is not reliable proof of identity. Whenever money transfer is mentioned, hang up immediately and call back using an old number stored in your contacts, or ask someone you both know. If the caller claims “poor signal” or “I’m in a meeting” and refuses a live video chat, treat it as a scam.
8-4.gain: The Cybersecurity Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security has outlined three key measures. First is motion verification: ask the other party to perform a smooth head-turn motion, or to completely cover their face with a palm and then remove it quickly. The original text notes that current AI technology still struggles to accurately simulate such complex facial occlusions and lighting changes, often resulting in choppy, blurry, or distorted images. Second is listening for audio cues: AI-generated voices sometimes lack natural breathing pauses or emotional variation, and may sound slightly mechanical or contain unusual background noise. Third and most important is cross-channel verification. As stated in the source material, “after hanging up, immediately call a number the person regularly uses and you recognize — do not call back the suspicious number — or ask a mutual acquaintance for confirmation.” The rule of thumb is: “Don’t trust video or voice alone; verify through actions and multiple channels.” Legally, using face-swapping or voice-cloning technology for fraud is strictly prohibited. Platforms must clearly label any service offering face generation, replacement, voice synthesis, or voice imitation; no organization or individual may remove, alter, or hide such labels. However, since scammers rarely follow these rules, the absence of a label cannot be taken as proof that the caller is genuine. The Criminal Investigation Bureau reported one case where a 14-member gang produced over 50000 synthetic face videos and collected more than 500000 pieces of personal information; police also seized 60 cloud servers nationwide. This labeling requirement took effect on September 1, 2025.
8-4.note: Always use an old number saved in your contacts when calling back — never dial the number shown on the incoming call or any new number the scammer provides. If the caller cites “poor signal” or “a meeting” to avoid a live video or motion test, assume it is a scam. Motion verification is only a supplementary tool; since AI capabilities keep improving, the only truly reliable step remains cross-channel confirmation. If money has already been transferred, refer to section 2 of this chapter and call 110 immediately to request a stop on the payment. For information on protecting your own facial and voice data, see section 14. This item is rated B because official sources provide identification methods and case examples, but no statistics are given on how much these measures actually reduce fraud rates. The main Ministry of Public Security website (mps.gov.cn) remains inaccessible due to a 521 error; the quoted texts from the Cybersecurity Bureau and Criminal Investigation Bureau were taken from a republishing page run by the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department.

8-5.t: If accused or summoned, hire a lawyer first — don’t settle privately or delete records
8-5.cost: Legal fees start at several thousand yuan. Those with financial difficulties can apply to legal aid agencies for a free lawyer. When questioned, answer only questions relevant to the case; leave the rest to your lawyer. The hard part is staying calm on the spot and resisting the urge to explain everything yourself.
8-5.human: You can hire a lawyer right from the first time you’re called in for questioning. If the lawyer requests a meeting, the detention center must arrange it within 48 hours, and those talks cannot be monitored. You’re allowed to refuse answering any questions unrelated to the case.
8-5.gain: Starting from the first interrogation or from the moment you’re placed under compulsory measures restricting your freedom, you have the right to appoint a lawyer. While the case remains under police investigation, only lawyers may represent you — no one else can serve as a defense counsel. Upon a lawyer’s request, the detention center must arrange a meeting within 48 hours, and such meetings are not monitored. No one may be forced to confess guilt, and you may refuse answering questions unrelated to the case. A summons or compulsory appearance lasts at most 12 hours; for especially serious and complex cases, this limit extends to 24 hours. A summons merely notifies you to come for questioning, while compulsory appearance means you’re physically taken there. Repeated summonses must not be used to detain someone indefinitely. Anyone fabricating facts to falsely accuse another and seeking criminal punishment for them faces up to three years in prison; if serious harm results, the sentence rises to three to ten years. If charges are dropped, prosecution is refused, or a court acquits you after detention or arrest, you may claim state compensation calculated daily based on the previous year’s national average wage for workers.
8-5.note: Do not attempt to settle privately with the other party or contact their family members. Any “private settlement” may be interpreted as admitting guilt. Chat logs, call records, and travel histories serve as proof of your innocence; deleting them removes your own evidence. If a report or accusation later proves unfounded, this does not constitute false accusation or entrapment. This rule applies equally to all accused individuals regardless of gender. For further details, see Section 33 (punishing those who fabricate facts), Section 34 (acquittal when evidence is insufficient and subsequent appeals), and Section 35 (daily state compensation after unlawful detention).

8-6.t: Coming forward voluntarily after an incident: Self‑surrender can cut a sentence by up to 40%, for minor offences the cut can be bigger or the penalty waived entirely, and the “statute of limitations” defense simply does not exist
8-6.cost: There is no cost at all. You can walk into a police station, stay on the scene and call the authorities, then tell them exactly what happened. The hard part is resisting the urge to “wait and see — maybe no one will notice.”
8-6.human: Voluntarily surrendering can reduce a prison term by up to 40%; for less serious offenses it may even lead to no punishment at all. If you confess only after being caught, the reduction is capped at 20%. Running away or denying responsibility yields no benefit. Relying on the statute of limitations to get off scot‑free is impossible: once a case is officially opened, the time you spend evading authorities does not count toward that limit. The relevant sentencing rules have been in effect since 2021.
8-6.gain: Article 67 of the Criminal Law states that anyone who voluntarily surrenders and truthfully confesses their crime receives a lighter or reduced sentence; those guilty of minor offenses may be exempted entirely. Even without surrender, a sincere confession can still earn a penalty cut; if it prevents especially grave consequences, the reduction can be even greater. Official sentencing guidelines set clear percentage ranges: voluntary surrender can lower the baseline sentence by up to 40% (or more for minor crimes), while a simple confession brings a reduction of up to 20%. Additional factors such as admitting to related, un‑discovered crimes or averting serious harm can add another 10‑50% cut. Plea agreements also grant up to 30% relief, and when combined with surrender, restitution, compensation and other mitigating circumstances the total reduction may exceed 60% (or even lead to full exemption for minor offenses). Conversely, the statute of limitations is divided into four tiers — 5, 10, 15 and 20 years — based on the maximum possible penalty (Article 87). However, Article 88 explicitly states that once an investigation or prosecution is underway, any attempt to evade it renders the time spent in hiding irrelevant; the clock never stops.
8-6.note: The primary beneficiary of this provision is the offender himself. Self‑surrender is a mitigating factor, not a blanket pardon; the exact reduction is left to judicial discretion, and stricter limits apply to violent and drug‑related crimes. Traffic‑accident cases follow a separate rule: staying at the scene, rendering aid and reporting the incident counts as voluntary surrender, yet because these actions are legally required, the permissible reduction is limited. Even if a driver flees first and later turns himself in, he still qualifies as a surrenderer; the baseline sentence used for calculation is the higher statutory maximum, and the subsequent reduction follows the same percentages described above (see Section 1 for proper post‑accident conduct: stop, help, call police). Consulting a lawyer does not conflict with a truthful confession; the attorney’s role is to verify that the written statement accurately reflects the facts, not to help fabricate a story.

8-7.t: Don’t touch the steering wheel after drinking — even for e‑bikes or “just moving the car a bit”
8-7.cost: Using a designated driver or taking a taxi costs only a few dozen yuan. Agree in advance who won’t drink at any gathering. It can be hard to politely refuse when others keep offering drinks.
8-7.human: Driving after drinking results in a 6‑month suspension of your license and a fine of 1000–2000 yuan. A second offense brings up to 10 days in jail and permanent license revocation. Drunk driving leads to immediate license cancellation; you can’t reapply for 5 years and may face criminal charges for dangerous driving, leaving a criminal record that affects background checks and certain jobs. Auto insurance won’t cover any claims: once you’ve been drinking, your policy becomes void. Even “just moving the car a bit” counts as driving.
8-7.gain: Temporary suspension of the license for 6 months and a fine ranging from 1000 to 2000 yuan for driving after drinking. Repeat offenders face up to 10 days in jail and permanent license revocation. Drunk driving results in immediate license cancellation; reapplication is prohibited for 5 years, and criminal liability for dangerous driving is pursued, leading to imprisonment and monetary penalties. For commercial drivers the penalties are harsher: 15 days in jail, a 5000‑yuan fine, and a 5‑year ban on driving commercially; drunk driving entails a 10‑year ban, after which they can never drive commercially again. If drinking or being drunk leads to a major accident and a criminal conviction, driving privileges are revoked for life. Commercial auto insurance policies explicitly exclude any claims arising from driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs (nationwide).
8-7.note: Drunk driving is a criminal offense that leaves a permanent record, affecting both background checks and eligibility for certain professions. The distinction between “drinking” and “being drunk” is defined by blood alcohol concentration levels set by national standards; this section does not verify those exact figures, so don’t guess where you fall on that scale.

8-8.t: Never lend your bank cards, SIM cards, or payment accounts to anyone — “money laundering” is not a side hustle
8-8.cost: Zero. Some people claim “just lend your card for a few transactions and you’ll get a few hundred yuan” — just say no.
8-8.human: Renting, lending, or selling your bank cards, SIM cards, or payment accounts is illegal on its own. Penalties include confiscation of all illegal earnings plus a fine of 1 to 10 times that amount; if no earnings were made, the maximum fine is 200000 yuan. In serious cases, offenders face up to 15 days in detention, a negative credit record, and restrictions on account functionality. If you knowingly assist criminals by receiving or transferring money using these accounts, you could be convicted of aiding information network criminal activities, punishable by up to 3 years in prison.
8-8.gain: Engaging in any activity that involves renting, lending, or selling phone cards, bank accounts, payment accounts, or internet accounts is illegal. Authorities confiscate all illegal earnings and impose a fine of 1 to 10 times that amount; if no earnings exist, the maximum fine is 200000 yuan. Serious violations lead to detention of up to 15 days, a negative credit record, account restrictions, and suspension of all non-counter banking services. Knowingly providing payment settlement assistance to criminals constitutes aiding information network criminal activities (known as “helping information network crimes”), punishable by up to 3 years in prison and a fine nationwide.
8-8.note: Claiming “I had no idea what the other person intended to do with my cards” won’t protect you. Law enforcement determines intent based on external circumstances: receiving payment for lending cards or unusually large transaction volumes can be used as evidence of awareness. Even if you ultimately aren’t convicted, accounts used to receive illicit funds get frozen and you face other penalties. Doing someone else’s real-name verification by face scan or by reading verification codes carries the same penalties; see item 45 (help with a face scan).

8-9.t: Checking your credit report twice a year for free helps spot any loans or cards you didn’t apply for
8-9.cost: It costs nothing. You can complete the check online in just ten minutes.
8-9.human: Laws give you the right to check your own credit report twice a year at no charge, and you can finish the process online in ten minutes. Negative entries stay on the report for five years from the date they’re resolved; after that they must be removed. If you dispute any information, the credit agency or data provider must respond to you in writing within 20 days. To check your report, use the official website of the People’s Bank of China’s Credit Information Center or your mobile banking app — avoid third‑party “credit check” apps, as they collect your personal data.
8-9.gain: Regulatory rules state that “individuals have the right to obtain their own credit reports twice a year free of charge,” meaning you can check your report twice annually at no cost. Negative records are kept for five years after the underlying issue is resolved; any older entries must be deleted. When you raise a dispute, the credit agency or source of the data must reply in writing within 20 days.
8-9.note: Identity theft leading to unauthorized loans or credit cards often goes unnoticed until a person is denied a mortgage years later. The proper channels for checking your report are the People’s Bank of China Credit Information Center website or mobile banking apps. Steer clear of third‑party “credit check” apps, as they harvest your personal information. If an acquaintance asked you to help scan your face or act as a witness for a loan, check your report again especially then; see item 45 (help with a face scan).

8-10.t: If a fight breaks out, call the police first — the one who strikes first almost always loses
8-10.cost: No cost at all. Simply move to a crowded area and call the police so the other person’s actions are captured on camera. The hard part is resisting the urge to shout back or push them.
8-10.human: Anyone who assaults another person faces 5 to 10 days in jail and a fine of 500 to 1000 yuan. If they act in a group, target the elderly, pregnant women, children, or disabled individuals, or repeat the assault multiple times, the penalty rises to 10 to 15 days in jail and a fine of 1000 to 2000 yuan. Causing minor injuries to another person turns it into a criminal case, punishable by up to 3 years in prison; serious injuries bring a sentence of 3 to 10 years. When two people fight each other, it does not qualify as self-defense — the person who strikes first almost always suffers the consequences. Moving to a crowded area and calling the police is far more effective than retaliating.
8-10.gain: Under the law, anyone who assaults another person or intentionally harms them faces 5 to 10 days in jail and a fine of 500 to 1000 yuan. Those who act in a group, target vulnerable groups, repeat the assault, or attack multiple people at once receive 10 to 15 days in jail and a fine of 1000 to 2000 yuan. Group fights are treated as hooliganism, carrying a maximum penalty of 15 days in jail and a 2000 yuan fine. Intentional bodily harm that meets criminal criteria results in up to 3 years in prison; serious injuries bring a sentence of 3 to 10 years. Legally, mutual fighting does not count as self-defense. However, if the other person strikes first and uses excessive force, or if you try to avoid the fight but they keep attacking, your retaliation is generally deemed lawful self-defense. Only when your response clearly exceeds what is necessary and causes major harm does it qualify as excessive self-defense, which still warrants a reduced or waived penalty (nationwide, effective January 1, 2026 under the Public Security Administration Punishment Law).
8-10.note: After the 2025 revision of the Public Security Administration Punishment Law, all article numbers changed; assault now falls under Article 51 instead of the old Article 43, so any older references are outdated. The definition of “minor injuries” used to determine criminal liability is set by official appraisal standards, which this section does not verify. If the aggressor is already on the ground or has fled, the threat ends, and any further retaliation is no longer considered self-defense.

8-11.t: You may defend yourself against an unavoidable attack, but only strike the person who is actually attacking — stop when he stops
8-11.cost: Legal fees start at several thousand yuan; those with financial difficulties may apply for legal aid. The main cost comes afterward: you’ll often be initially charged with intentional injury, required to cooperate with investigations, and sometimes detained for up to ten days. The challenge is staying composed during this period.
8-11.human: To protect yourself or others from an ongoing attack, it is legally acceptable to intervene and injure the attacker. If someone is committing murder, robbery, rape, kidnapping, or any other violent crime, harming or even killing them is not considered excessive. However, you must only strike the person actively attacking — stop as soon as he ceases. Even if the court ultimately rules in your favor, the process is far from easy; many people are first charged and detained for several days. In total, 47 individuals have been recognized as acting in self-defense under these circumstances.
8-11.gain: Criminal law defines what constitutes legitimate self-defense. When national interests, public welfare, or your own or another person’s life, property, and other rights are under unlawful attack, intervening to injure the aggressor qualifies as self-defense and carries no criminal liability. The law also states: “If self-defense clearly exceeds necessary limits and causes serious harm, criminal responsibility applies, though punishment may be mitigated or waived.” Additionally: “In cases of ongoing violent crimes such as murder, robbery, rape, kidnapping, or other acts seriously threatening personal safety, any defensive actions resulting in injury or death of the aggressor do not constitute excessive defense and incur no criminal liability.” Official guidelines further clarify these boundaries: both “clearly exceeding necessary limits” and “causing serious harm” must be present for it to be deemed excessive; causing only minor injuries does not count. Defense must be directed solely at the aggressor; using lethal force against minor offenses is not permitted. Real-world examples include the Yu Haiming case (2018), where initial charges were later dropped after a ruling of self-defense, and the Chen case, where a student’s defensive actions were similarly recognized as lawful. A total of 45 cases have been officially documented as falling under this category.
8-11.note: The default course of action remains as described in item 10: retreat and call the police. Fighting back when two parties are already engaged does not qualify as defense, nor does pursuing an attacker after he has fled or fallen. This provision applies only when retreat is impossible; it does not encourage violence. Afterward, three steps are crucial: remain at the scene after calling police, preserve any surveillance footage and witnesses, and consult a lawyer before any police questioning. If charges are eventually dropped or you are acquitted, you may seek state compensation for detention days, as outlined in item 35. Defending others is also legally permitted, though intervening in unrelated fights without preparation carries different risks, as discussed in item 13. This protection primarily benefits you and your family.

8-12.t: Who to hold accountable — unpaid wages, wrongful dismissal, financial losses — filing complaints, arbitration, or lawsuits instead of taking revenge
8-12.cost: There are no fees for filing complaints or arbitration. However, you’ll need to make one or two trips and wait several months. The real challenge is resisting the urge to take matters into your own hands during that time.
8-12.human: Pursuing legal channels may ultimately leave you without any compensation. On the other hand, resorting to revenge achieves the same result — no money recovered — while also risking your own life. Consider the case in Wuxi: Xu failed to obtain his diploma and was dissatisfied with his internship pay, so he attacked people with a knife, killing 8 and injuring 17. He was sentenced to death, which was carried out. Nationwide in 2024, 654,000 workers recovered 8.65 billion yuan through complaints and arbitration for unpaid wages.
8-12.gain: Official statistics back up legal remedies. In 2024, labor inspectors handled 137,000 cases, resulting in 8.65 billion yuan being returned to 654,000 workers. Additionally, 998 individuals were convicted under laws against wage theft. Instructions on filing labor complaints and arbitration are provided in Section 7, Item 2. The consequences of revenge are outlined in Article 232 of the Criminal Law: “Whoever intentionally kills another shall be sentenced to death, life imprisonment, or fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years; if the circumstances are relatively minor, they shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years.” An official example: Xu failed his exams and did not receive his diploma; he also resented his internship pay. On November 16, 2024, he returned to Wuxi Arts and Crafts Vocational College and attacked people with a knife, killing 8 and injuring 17. He was sentenced to death for intentional homicide, with political rights revoked for life; the sentence was carried out on January 20, 2025. His grievances concerned the school and pay, yet his victims were fellow students, and he received no compensation at all (nationwide data).
8-12.note: Interns still enrolled in school generally do not qualify as having an employment relationship with their host organizations. If they fail to receive internship pay, they must seek mediation from their school or file a lawsuit in court, as labor arbitration is not an option. The same applies to individuals who perform private work for families or individuals and are then denied payment — they must also turn to the courts; see Section 7, Item 22 (first determine who hired you). Detailed steps for filing labor complaints and arbitration are provided in Section 7, Item 2. The limits on debt collection are outlined in Section 9, Item 15 (no detaining or confining debtors). Even legal channels may fail to secure compensation, as case resolution does not guarantee payment receipt. Conversely, revenge achieves no financial recovery and risks your own life.

8-13.t: No matter how angry you are, never target innocent people: deliberately driving into a crowd or committing violence in public is classified as endangering public safety by dangerous means, carrying a minimum sentence of three years; if anyone dies, the sentence starts at ten years and goes up to death
8-13.cost: There is no monetary cost involved. The real challenge is suppressing such impulses when you’re enraged.
8-13.human: Intentionally driving into a crowd or attacking people in public constitutes endangering public safety by dangerous means. Even if no one is injured, the offender still faces at least three years in prison. If fatalities occur, the sentence rises to ten years or more, life imprisonment, or death. In the Zhuhai case, Fan Weiqiu, dissatisfied with the divorce settlement, drove his car into a crowd exercising at a sports center, resulting in 35 deaths and 43 injuries; he was sentenced to death and executed.
8-13.gain: Article 114 of the Criminal Law states: “Whoever commits arson, breaches a dike, causes an explosion, releases toxic, radioactive, or infectious agents, or endangers public safety by any other dangerous means, without causing serious consequences, shall be sentenced to three to ten years in prison.” Thus, even when no injuries occur, the minimum penalty is three years. Article 115 adds that if serious injury, death, or major property damage results, the sentence becomes ten years or more, life imprisonment, or death. Official case example: Fan Weiqiu, disillusioned by his failed marriage and unhappy with the divorce terms, resolved to vent his anger by driving into a crowd. On the evening of November 11, 2024, he crashed his vehicle into exercisers at Zhuhai Sports Center, killing 35 and injuring 43. He was convicted under the aforementioned article and sentenced to death, with political rights revoked; the sentence was carried out on January 20, 2025 after Supreme Court approval. His grievance pertained solely to the divorce ruling; his victims were completely unrelated runners from across the country.
8-13.note: Expressing thoughts like “I don’t want to live anyway” does not serve as a mitigating factor in sentencing. The Supreme People’s Court’s 2025 work report emphasizes “resolutely punishing with severity, speed, and strictness those who outrageously violate legal and moral boundaries.” Merely threatening to commit acts such as arson, explosions, or poisoning that endanger public safety and disrupt order can lead to detention from five to ten days and a fine of up to 1000 yuan under the Public Security Administration Punishment Law (effective January 1, 2026). Similarly, sending threatening letters or otherwise endangering another’s safety is illegal, punishable by up to five days’ detention or a similar fine. Anyone entertaining such ideas should refer to item 14, which treats notions like “finding a scapegoat” as a medical emergency requiring immediate intervention.

8-14.t: Thoughts such as “find a scapegoat” or “die together” must be treated as a medical emergency: leave the scene, hand over car keys and knives to someone else, and call 12356
8-14.cost: There is no monetary cost. The difficulty lies in admitting that something is wrong at the moment and in handing over control of dangerous items to another person.
8-14.human: The window between the first appearance of such thoughts and any attempt to act on them is very short. Among 82 people who survived a suicide attempt, 47.6% reported that no more than 10 minutes passed from the first thought to taking action. Therefore, the goal is not to “figure things out” intellectually, but to create physical distance between oneself and potential lethal tools — steering wheel, knife, gas valve, rope — and simply endure those ten minutes. After that, call 12356.
8-14.gain: This brief window between thought and action is well documented. In interviews conducted within three days of admission, 47.6% of those 82 individuals stated that the interval from initial thought to execution was under 10 minutes. A systematic review spanning ten years shows growing evidence that restricting access to lethal means reduces suicide rates. For instance, after tighter controls on painkillers, suicide rates linked to them dropped by 43%. After installing protective barriers at popular suicide sites, rates fell by 86% (ranging from 79% to 91%). Creating that ten‑minute buffer by removing lethal objects is precisely what this advice aims to achieve. 12356 is the national mental health helpline, operating at least 18 hours per day nationwide as of May 1, 2025.
8-14.note: This grade is assigned because both pieces of evidence derive from suicide‑research literature and have not been directly tested in contexts involving impulses to harm others. The Deisenhammer study involved only 82 participants at a single hospital. When feeling unwell, avoid driving or taking shifts where you bear responsibility for others’ safety; hand over duties first. For those having thoughts of self‑harm, see Section 1, Item 25 (call 12356 when suicidal). For coping strategies during low mood, see Section 3, Item 18.

8-15.t: Family members say “no one will be safe” or “I’ll take the kids and leave” — don’t dismiss this as anger: close relatives can take such a person to the hospital, and police must respond to any emergency call
8-15.cost: Registration and consultation fees range from a few dozen to several hundred yuan. Accompanying the person to the hospital takes half a day to a full day. The real challenge is getting them to agree to go.
8-15.human: When family members say things like “no one will be safe” or “I’ll take the kids and leave,” close relatives have the right to take that person to a hospital, where treatment cannot be refused. If there has already been violence or an imminent risk of harm, hospitalization does not require the person’s consent. If it’s unclear whether these statements are just angry outbursts or genuine threats, call 12356 for advice or dial 110 so police can intervene. Keeping this information secret does not help the person at all.
8-15.gain: Article 28, paragraph 2 of the Mental Health Law states: “When a suspected mental disorder patient exhibits behavior that harms themselves or others, or shows a clear risk of doing so, their close relatives, employer, or local police must act immediately to stop such behavior and arrange transport to a medical facility for diagnosis.” The same article also requires hospitals to accept and diagnose any such patients without refusal. Article 29 mandates that hospitals admit these individuals right away, assign a licensed psychiatrist for evaluation, and issue a diagnosis promptly. Article 30 says voluntary admission is the norm, except in cases where the diagnosis confirms a severe mental disorder accompanied by actual or imminent harm to others — in such cases, involuntary hospitalization is permitted. Making threats of violence is grounds for calling 110. Writing threatening letters or using other means to endanger someone’s safety can result in detention for up to five days or a fine of up to 1000 yuan. Those who threaten to commit arson, explosions, or other acts endangering public safety face detention from five to ten days and a similar fine (effective January 1, 2026 under China’s Public Security Administration Punishment Law).
8-15.note: This guidance applies to spouses, parents, and children living in the same household. The phrase “no one will be safe” clearly includes the speaker, and the law grants this right specifically to close relatives — outsiders cannot intervene without police involvement. This rule targets genuine danger signs, not angry remarks during arguments or attempts to force uncooperative family members into treatment. Conversely, Article 35 states that if further evaluation proves the person does not have a serious mental disorder, they must be released from the hospital. When in doubt, call 12356 or 110. If you cannot tell whether someone is thinking of suicide, you can simply ask: asking does not make them more likely to act (Section 1, Item 43: asking people close to you who seem off). The investigation into Germanwings Flight 9525 revealed that authorities and employers could not prevent the co-pilot from flying that day because “neither he nor anyone else — doctors, colleagues, or family — informed them of his condition.” All 150 people on board perished: two pilots, four flight attendants, and 144 passengers. Keeping such risks hidden is never helpful.

8-16.t: Don’t curse, spread rumors, or share unverified content online; if you’re a victim of online abuse, document evidence first then report it to police
8-16.cost: No cost at all. Just take ten extra seconds to think before posting. When attacked, take screenshots, record video, save links and account IDs, file a complaint with the platform first, then report it to police. The hardest part is resisting the urge to fire back when being cursed at.
8-16.human: Publicly cursing, spreading rumors or defaming others can result in detention for up to 5 days or a fine of up to 1000 yuan; for more serious cases, detention ranges from 5 to 10 days. If the circumstances are especially grave, it constitutes the crimes of insult or defamation, punishable by up to 3 years in prison. Simply sharing such content also makes you liable. Conversely, if you’re a victim of online abuse, you generally have to file a lawsuit in court yourself to pursue legal action for insult or defamation, so you must rely on yourself to take screenshots, record video and save links.
8-16.gain: Those who openly insult others or fabricate facts to defame them face detention for up to 5 days or a fine of up to 1000 yuan; for more serious cases, detention ranges from 5 to 10 days.
