16-4.human: For cancers that are otherwise treatable, using only alternative therapy and skipping standard surgery, chemo, radiotherapy, and hormone treatment carries about 2.5 times the death risk of standard care. People who add complementary therapy while on standard treatment more often refuse chemo or radiotherapy mid-course, and the extra deaths show up there. Some herbs weaken anti-rejection or anticoagulant drugs; ask your treating doctor before taking anything.
16-4.gain: Two US cancer-registry studies looked at non-metastatic, potentially curable breast, prostate, lung, and colorectal cancer. The first compared patients who used only alternative therapy and did none of surgery, chemo/radiotherapy, or endocrine treatment with matched standard-care patients: death risk 2.5-fold (HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.88–3.27, about 1.5 times higher). Breast cancer 5.68-fold (3.22–10.04), lung 2.17-fold (1.42–3.32), colorectal 4.57-fold (1.66–12.61). The second looked at standard treatment plus complementary therapy: refusal rates were surgery 7.0% vs 0.1%, chemo 34.1% vs 3.2%, radiotherapy 53.0% vs 2.3%, endocrine therapy 33.7% vs 2.8%. Five-year survival 82.2% vs 86.6%; death risk 2.08-fold (HR 2.08, 1.50–2.90, about double). After accounting for delay and refusal, complementary therapy alone was not linked to death (HR 1.39, 0.83–2.33). The author’s conclusion: extra deaths came from refusing standard treatment. China’s State Administration for Market Regulation requires health-food labels to state: “Health food is not medicine and cannot replace drugs to treat disease.” The US National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH) states that St John’s wort (贯叶连翘) weakens several drugs, including cyclosporine for transplant rejection and the anticoagulant warfarin
16-4.note: B only. Both studies were cancer-only, registry follow-up without randomized groups; people who chose alternative therapy may differ in other ways. Stopping meds in hypertension or diabetes: see item 1 (full adherence). Tell your treating doctor before any supplement. Whether to pay for supplements: Section 6, item 10 (supplements, tonic formulas, tonics)

16-5.t: When a chronic condition is stable, a community health center can dispense up to 12 weeks of medication at once
16-5.cost: No cost. At the community health service center (社区卫生服务中心), ask in one sentence whether long-term prescriptions are available.
16-5.human: If the illness is stable and the drug regimen unchanged, the community center can supply enough for 12 weeks in one visit. That saves half a day each month queuing at a large hospital for a refill. Within the same pooled insurance region (统筹地区), inpatient reimbursement at primary-level facilities is usually about ten percentage points higher than at the next tier up.
16-5.gain: Avoids monthly trips to a large hospital just to refill. In the same pooled insurance region, inpatient reimbursement at primary-level facilities is in principle about ten percentage points higher than at the next tier
16-5.note: “Eligible” is judged by the doctor—usually clear diagnosis and stable regimen. Same drugs; what you save is half a day and registration fees each month. If the community site lacks your drug, ask about shortage registration and delivery. The same policy also asks tertiary hospitals to gradually cut routine outpatient for such chronic diseases and shift those specialists’ general clinics to community sites. Using big hospitals mainly as refill points will get harder to book over time.

16-6.t: Before signing a family doctor (家庭医生) contract at community level, ask which services are covered by yibao (医保) and which are out of pocket
16-6.cost: No cost. One extra minute of questions before signing.
16-6.human: The basic service package is paid by yibao (医保) as required. Personalized service packages are entirely self-paid. When someone sells an “upgrade package,” ask whether it is basic or personalized, whether it is filed with the county health authority, and the yearly price.
16-6.gain: Basic service package is paid by yibao (医保) per rules. Personalized packages are fully self-paid and must be filed with the county-level health administration (县级卫生健康部门)
16-6.note: The value of signing is long-term follow-up for your condition, not how many items are bundled. When offered an “upgrade package,” ask three things: basic or personalized, filed or not, and cost per year.

16-7.t: After a diabetes diagnosis, get a dilated eye exam once, then on the interval your doctor sets; check feet once a year
16-7.cost: One dilated eye exam costs from a few dozen to a few hundred CNY. Foot exams are usually part of outpatient visits without extra charge. The hard part is remembering when eyes and feet feel fine.
16-7.human: Diabetes damage to the retina and feet rarely hurts or feels wrong until vision fails or ulcers appear. Early detection still allows treatment. Type 2 diabetes: dilated eye exam at diagnosis; type 1: start five years after onset. After one or two normal exams with blood sugar at target, spacing can widen to every one or two years. Feet: once a year.
16-7.gain: Retinal damage from diabetes is diabetic retinopathy; foot damage is diabetic foot. Both are nearly silent until late. Early detection still allows treatment. By the time vision is lost or the foot breaks down, it is late
16-7.note: Type 2: exam at diagnosis; type 1: five years after onset, because type 2 often ran high for years unnoticed. After one or two normal exams with sugar at target, every 1–2 years may suffice. If foot sensation is dull, inspect the sole daily, mirror if needed.

16-8.t: After kidney stones, drink 2.5–3 liters of water daily and keep salt under 6 g
16-8.cost: No cost. Make drinking water a habit. Sweaty days need more; the hard part is remembering every day.
16-8.human: After a first calcium stone, about one in four will get another within five years if nothing is done. Drinking enough daily cuts five-year recurrence to a bit over one in ten—roughly half less. UK guidance suggests 2.5–3 L water daily and salt under 6 g.
16-8.gain: A 5-year randomized trial in 199 patients with a first calcium stone and no identified cause (idiopathic calcium nephrolithiasis). One group drank at least 2 L water daily; the other had no intervention. Recurrence in 5 years: water group 12/99 (12.1%), control 27/100 (27.0%), P=0.008. Smaller P means the gap is less likely chance. Mean time to recurrence: 38.7±13.2 months vs 25.1±16.4 months, P=0.016. Baseline 24-hour urine volume in stone patients was clearly lower than in people without stones: men 1,057±238 mL vs 1,401±562 mL (P<0.0001), women 990±230 mL vs 1,239±440 mL (P<0.001). NICE guideline NG118 section 1.8.1 advises adults 2.5–3 L water daily; children and adolescents 1–2 L by age. Fresh lemon juice in water is fine; avoid carbonated drinks; adults keep salt under 6 g daily
16-8.note: Recurrence falls by about 55% at no cost—by this book’s ranking, the best value in this section. Track 24-hour urine volume, target 2–2.5 L or more, not just fluid swallowed. Heavy sweaters and hot environments need more. The trial was first-episode idiopathic calcium stones; uric acid, infection, and cystine stones need different plans. After recurrence, stone composition analysis and 24-hour urine are worth doing before adding drugs. Do not cut calcium to prevent stones—Section 6, item 21. Severe flank or abdominal colic needs hospital care, not flushing with water. Painless blood in urine has other workup—Section 1, item 27

16-9.t: After gout diagnosis, take urate-lowering therapy long term; keep serum urate below 360 µmol/L and maintain it
16-9.cost: Allopurinol (别嘌醇) costs a few to a few dozen CNY per month. At first check serum urate every few weeks to titrate dose; once stable, every few months. For the first 3–6 months add anti-inflammatory prophylaxis. The hard part is continuing when there is no pain.
16-9.human: Gout needs long-term urate-lowering drugs to hold urate below 360 µmol/L; painkillers alone when flaring are not enough. In one trial, nurses titrated dose from labs: 95% at target at 2 years vs 30% with usual GP care. Do not stop once at target. Diet alone rarely reaches that line; stopping alcohol lowers urate only 1.6 mg/dL.
16-9.gain: Randomized trial, 517 adults with a flare in the past 12 months. One group had nurse-led education and treat-to-target urate titration; the other usual GP care. At 2 years, proportion with serum urate <360 µmol/L (6 mg/dL): 95% vs 30%. Likelihood of target vs usual care: RR 3.18, 95% CI 2.42–4.18, P<0.0001. Secondary outcomes at year 2—flare frequency, tophi, quality of life—also favored the nurse-led group. Each extra quality-adjusted life year gained cost £5,066. Follow-up survey: 438 invited, 82% response; both groups self-reported flares in the past 12 months. Target group median 0 (interquartile range 0–0); usual care 1 (0–3), P<0.001. Still on urate-lowering therapy: adjusted RR 1.19 (1.09–1.30) in the target group. 2020 American College of Rheumatology gout guideline strongly recommends urate-lowering therapy for tophi, imaging bone erosion from gout, or ≥2 flares per year: monitor serum urate, titrate to target <6 mg/dL; first-line allopurinol, including CKD stage 3+, start ≤100 mg/day. Give anti-inflammatory prophylaxis at initiation for at least 3–6 months. The same guideline cites case series: after long good control, some stopped drugs yet kept urate <7 mg/dL; only 13% (27/211) had zero flares over 5 years. Diet: limiting or stopping alcohol vs not limiting lowered urate 1.6 mg/dL; one beer raised urate 0.16 mg/dL; healthy, Mediterranean, and DASH patterns had smaller effects. First-line drug choice is disputed. ACR strongly recommends allopurinol for efficacy at adequate dose, tolerability, safety, and cost; conditionally suggests switching febuxostat (非布司他) if cardiovascular disease or new cardiovascular events and alternatives exist—aligned with FDA boxed warning on febuxostat. CARES trial: 6,190 gout patients with cardiovascular disease randomized to febuxostat or allopurinol. All-cause death risk febuxostat vs allopurinol HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01–1.47 (about 22% higher); cardiovascular death 1.34 (1.03–1.73, about 34% higher). European FAST trial differed: 6,128 patients ≥60 with cardiovascular risk factors; major cardiovascular events on febuxostat not higher than allopurinol (HR 0.85, 0.70–1.03). Deaths febuxostat 7.2%, allopurinol 8.6%. For uricosurics, ACR conditionally advises against urine alkalinization—no evidence, very low certainty—while stressing more fluids; avoid uricosurics if known nephrolithiasis or CKD stage 3+

17-1.t: While the elder is still lucid, name a future guardian in writing
17-1.cost: A few hundred CNY at a notary office (公证处) for one document. One conversation with the elder can settle it. The hard part is bringing it up: you have to talk face to face about the day they will no longer be able to manage for themselves.
17-1.human: While the elder’s mind is still clear, spend a few hundred yuan at a notary office on a written document that names who will be their guardian later. Without it, once they cannot decide for themselves, a court decides who signs for them and who handles their money. If family disagree, that takes even longer.
17-1.gain: The Civil Code (民法典) lets lucid adults who can decide for themselves (legally, adults with full capacity for civil conduct (具有完全民事行为能力的成年人)) agree in advance who will be their guardian. That person can be a close relative or any willing individual or organization. The agreement must determine the guardian in writing (以书面形式确定自己的监护人). When they later cannot decide at all, or can decide only in part (lose or partially lose capacity for civil conduct (丧失或者部分丧失民事行为能力)), the named person takes charge. Without that document, who signs and who manages money goes through court appointment.
17-1.note: This is voluntary guardianship (意定监护)—someone you choose yourself in advance. That person ranks ahead of the default statutory guardianship order. Elders living alone, with children far away, or in complicated family situations need this more. Having it notarized at a notary office is recommended.

17-2.t: Make a will; later ones override earlier ones, and notarized wills no longer rank first
17-2.cost: Handwriting a will yourself costs nothing. Notarization at a notary office (公证处) runs from a few hundred to over a thousand CNY. The hard part is bringing it up: you must discuss end-of-life matters with family.
17-2.human: The law recognizes six types of will, but one formal mistake voids the whole document—that is the most common failure. For a fully handwritten will, the testator must write every word, sign, and date it. If several wills conflict, the last one controls. Since 2021, a notarized will no longer automatically ranks above the others.
17-2.gain: The Civil Code (民法典) accepts six will forms: wholly handwritten, written by another person, printed, audio/video, oral, and notarized. Each has required formal steps (形式要件). If multiple wills conflict, the last one prevails. Since 2021, a notarized will no longer automatically ranks first.
17-2.note: For a wholly handwritten will, the testator must write every word, sign, and date it. A printed will needs at least two witnesses. Testator and witnesses must sign every page and date them. Heirs, people named to receive property, and their close relatives cannot serve as witnesses. Wrong form voids the whole will—that is the most common failure.

17-3.t: Keep the elder’s money in a separate account; set a two-person rule for large spending
17-3.cost: No cost. Talk once with family and pick a dollar threshold. The hard part is how to bring it up so the elder does not feel you are guarding against them.
17-3.human: Scammers often give small gifts and warm attention first, build trust, then take a large sum at once. They often say “do not tell anyone.” Agree in advance: spending above a set amount must be cleared with a specific person first. That way the family knows, and paying is delayed.
17-3.gain: In 2022 elder-fraud case releases, the Supreme People’s Procuratorate (最高检) said these crimes use small favors and feigned kinship to gain trust, then false claims and promised high returns to take large sums. In one case, a fake collectibles firm sent staff to clean and chat with elders and even take them as “godparents.” Goods were sealed in black bags with orders not to open them so family would not see. The firm took more than 1.92 million CNY; the boss received 7 years 6 months for fund-raising fraud. Beijing’s local financial regulator warned in 2023 not to believe “do not tell anyone.” When unsure, consult family, children, and trusted neighbors before investing. U.S. Federal Trade Commission totals reported by people aged 60+ rose from about USD 600 million in 2020 to about USD 2.4 billion in 2024, driven mainly by single losses over USD 100,000. Agreeing that “spending above X must be cleared with someone first” lets the family know before money moves and pushes the decision back.
17-3.note: No study has measured how much less fraud families see with this rule. Grade B because the scam pattern and “consult family more” come from procuratorial and financial regulators, same nature as entry 6 (housing-for-pension). Excitement makes people easier to persuade—see entry 4 (“I need to go home and talk with my family”). General anti-fraud rules are in Section 8 and Section 13. Do not frame it as “afraid you’ll be scammed”; “we track household money in one place” is easier for elders to accept. Do not take all of an elder’s money into a child’s custody—that triggers a different kind of dispute.

17-4.t: Give the elder a line they can always use: “I need to go home and talk with my family”
17-4.cost: No cost. One conversation, a few minutes.
17-4.human: Sales pitches and fraud rely on on-the-spot pressure so you pay before you can think. When people are excited, exaggerated ads land harder; elders are more swayed than younger adults. Agree on “I need to go home and talk with my family” in advance. They can say it anytime, save face on the spot, and decide after they cool down at home.
17-4.gain: Pitches and fraud both lean on live pressure. The U.S. Federal Trade Commission anti-scam guide says scammers want action before you can think. On phone calls they tell you not to hang up so you cannot verify. The guide says tell someone—a friend, family member, or neighbor—before you act; saying it aloud may expose the scam. The former China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (银保监会) risk notice in 2021 also told elders to consult family before buying wealth products. One experiment enrolled 116 people aged 65–85 and 115 aged 30–40. Researchers used a win/loss game to stir some people’s emotions, then showed exaggerated ads. Those whose emotions were stirred wanted to buy more. Regardless of arousal, elders wanted to buy more than younger adults. Authors advise waiting until emotions settle before spending. Another experiment enrolled people previously cheated by mail fraud, mostly older. Without prior warning, nearly half agreed outright to a simulated telemarketing scam call. With a reminder call two to four weeks ahead, far fewer agreed outright. Agreeing on “I need to go home and talk with my family” gives the elder an exit without deciding on the spot.
17-4.note: Grade B because neither experiment tested this exact sentence. One tested buying urge when emotional; one tested whether advance warning helps—no study compared fraud rates for elders who had this line ready. Use together with entry 3 (separate account and two-person rule). Do fall-prevention fixes at home too—see Section 1. The line is a face-saving exit, not a way to control them. When surrounded by sales staff, speaking up to refuse in front of a room is often harder than judging whether the pitch is true.

17-5.t: Avoid any “invest in elder care” scheme that makes the elder pay first: cards, beds, elder apartments, travel elder care, and conference sales are the same illegal fund-raising pattern
17-5.cost: No cost. Read the list below to the elder once—minutes. Then refuse outright: no lectures, no site visits, no leaving a phone number. Hard if they already went several times and know the promoters.
17-5.human: Any elder-care label that takes money upfront and promises returns is the same scam: membership cards, bed reservations, elder apartments, travel elder care, conference sales of elder products. Under the rules, losses from this kind of fund-raising are borne by participants themselves. One case raised CNY 136 million by “pre-booking elder apartment beds,” harming more than 2,100 people. The only step you can block is paying.
17-5.gain: The Ministry of Civil Affairs (民政部) lists five patterns—recognize the label, not the person. (1) Fake elder-service agencies: no real entity, rented venue, claiming a cooperation deal with a licensed home to “piggyback.” (2) “Elder services”: VIP/membership/prepaid cards, prepaid “service fees,” promises beyond bed capacity. (3) “Elder investment”: stakes in wellness bases, fake elder apartments, long-term bed leases, “time bank” mutual aid, with buyback, leaseback, or repurchase promises. (4) “Elder products”: buyback, consignment, consumption rebates, free exams, gifts, conference marketing, wellness talks, “expert” clinics. (5) “Travel elder care”: cheap or free tours, stored-value rebates, points-based elder care. Recovery is ruled out in the regulations. Article 25 of the Regulations on Prevention and Disposal of Illegal Fund-raising (防范和处置非法集资条例): “Losses suffered from participating in illegal fund-raising shall be borne by the participants themselves.” Reported cases: Dai et al. raised CNY 136 million via pre-booked elder apartment beds, more than 2,100 victims; Dai received 15 years and a CNY 400,000 fine for fund-raising fraud. Cao raised CNY 13.207 billion in the name of elder-industry investment, involving more than 110,000 people—life imprisonment, deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property. Health-product conference sales were prosecuted as fraud: Ni used free meals, gifts, and chauffeured rides to pull elders into lectures; speakers used fake personas, fake cases, and inflated “discounts” to claim anti-cancer effects. Elders paid dozens of times cost for “dihydroquercetin”; sales exceeded CNY 620,000. Ni received 10 years 3 months and a CNY 120,000 fine (nationwide; regulations effective 2021-05-01).
17-5.note: Judge by “pay first” and “promised returns,” not “looks legitimate.” Licensed homes sell services; once the pitch adds investment, rebates, or payback, do not trust it. Lectures, tours, and free clinics are not illegal and are hard to stop—the step you can stop is payment, together with entry 3’s two-person rule. If money was already paid, immediately follow Section 8 entry 2: call 110 or 96110 for payment stop, and report to the local lead agency for illegal fund-raising. “Housing-for-pension” is a separate path—see entry 6 (housing reverse mortgage insurance).

17-6.t: Except insurers’ housing reverse mortgage insurance, avoid all other “housing-for-pension” pitches; never mortgage the home to buy wealth products
17-6.cost: No cost. Keep the property deed at home; do not hand it to anyone pitching “housing-for-pension” (以房养老). Show mortgage, guarantee, and loan contracts to your children before signing. Hard when door-to-door promoters are warm and keep coming back—the elder feels rude saying no.
17-6.human: The legitimate form is only housing reverse mortgage insurance (住房反向抵押养老保险) from insurers, still in pilot. Door-to-door pitches are unrelated: they trick elders into mortgaging the house, then using the loan to buy recommended wealth products. Some did not know the home was mortgaged and ended with no house plus debt.
17-6.gain: The former CBIRC Consumer Protection Bureau (银保监会消保局) separated real from fake. The real product is “housing reverse mortgage insurance for older persons.” Elders with full legal title mortgage the home to the insurer; they keep living in it, using it, and collecting rent. Sale or disposal needs the mortgagee (insurer) to agree. They receive pension payments under the contract until death. The business remains pilot-scale with few participants. Fraudsters’ “housing-for-pension” is “completely unrelated” to the state pilot and is “using national policy as cover to promote illegal fund-raising.” The method is tricking elders into mortgage, then buying recommended products—“often a Ponzi scheme of paying old debts with new money.” The notice quotes consequences: “Some participants did not even know their property was mortgaged; they ultimately lost the house and still owed the loan.” It also gives yield lines: “If a wealth product promises returns above 6%, question it; above 8% is very dangerous; above 10%, prepare to lose all principal; ‘guaranteed high yield’ is financial fraud.” The same notice requires careful contract signing and not signing blank contracts (nationwide, June 2021).
17-6.note: Grade B because these lines come from regulator risk notices and judgment, not research. The 6%, 8%, and 10% lines are consumer reference points, not statutory thresholds. CBIRC was merged into the National Administration of Financial Regulation (国家金融监督管理总局); the original page may be unavailable—provincial financial regulator reposts are cited. Wealth loss is secondary; after the home is mortgaged the elder may still owe a large loan—loss exceeds principal. General rules on signing and blank contracts: Section 8 entry 17. After fraud: payment stop, Section 8 entry 2.

17-7.t: If an elder is bedbound long term or severely disabled, apply for long-term care insurance (长期护理保险) at the local basic medical insurance (医保) office—it is not only for the elderly
17-7.cost: One trip to the local medical insurance office where you are enrolled, plus one disability-level assessment. If you pass the first assessment, the fund pays the assessment fee—no out-of-pocket cost.
17-7.human: Long-term care insurance helps pay for hired care. If someone at home is severely disabled for at least about six months, apply at the local medical insurance office. Eligible care fees need not be paid upfront first; roughly 70% is reimbursed for employee enrollees and about 50% for urban/rural resident enrollees; bed and meal charges are not covered. There is no age floor—young people with severe disability can apply too.
17-7.gain: Covered long-term care service fees have no deductible (起付线)—you do not need to pay a threshold amount before reimbursement starts. For those enrolled under the employee policy, the fund reimburses about 70%. For those enrolled under the non-employed urban/rural resident policy, about 50%. The annual cap (年度最高支付限额) is at most 50% of the prior year’s per-capita disposable income of urban/rural residents in the local pooling area.
17-7.note: Disability must be “long-term and ongoing (generally 6 months or more)”—a few weeks in hospital does not qualify. There is also a 6-month waiting period before benefits start. Bed fees, meals, and similar non-care costs are not paid. Medical costs that basic medical insurance should cover are not paid by long-term care insurance. Those already receiving work-injury living-care benefits do not double-dip. This is separate paperwork and money from the disability care subsidy in the two disability subsidies (两项补贴)—no conflict; see Section 7 entry 8. Home and community care often get higher reimbursement rates; institutional care is not required. The program rolls out by locality with different assessment standards. Call 12393 or the local medical insurance handler first to ask whether it is live locally and how to book assessment. If assessment fails, reapply if disability worsens.

17-8.t: If someone is bedbound long term, treat pressure ulcers as enemy number one: electric alternating-pressure mattress, scheduled turning, daily check of bony prominences
17-8.cost: Home electric alternating-pressure air mattresses start at a few hundred CNY. One turn takes minutes. The hard part is turning every two to three hours, including at night—one caregiver cannot sustain that alone.
17-8.human: Among elders who already had pressure ulcers before hip-fracture surgery, the chance of dying within 30 days was about one-fifth higher. An electric air mattress cut new ulcers by about 60%. Turning on schedule, done for real, cut risk by about 70%. Do not leave someone prone for long stretches. Check sacrum, heels, hips, and shoulder/back daily; if pressure leaves red that does not blanch, contact a nurse or doctor the same day.
17-8.gain: 19,520 hip-fracture surgery patients (U.S. NSQIP 2016–2019). Those with preoperative pressure ulcers had higher 30-day mortality. After adjusting for other factors the association held (OR 1.2, 21% higher odds, P=0.004). They also had more complications: deep vein thrombosis (OR 1.59), pneumonia (OR 1.39), unplanned readmission (OR 1.43), and 0.4 more hospital days on average. 324 hospitalized elders (mean age 86), median follow-up 18 months. Pressure ulcers independently predicted long-term death (HR 1.500, 95% CI 1.059 to 2.126, P=0.020)—meaning after other factors were removed, ulcers alone predicted outcome. Network meta-analysis of 65 randomized trials compared active air support surfaces to standard hospital mattresses. Active air surfaces (electric air mattresses) had lower pressure-ulcer incidence (RR 0.42, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.63, moderate certainty). Mixed active air: RR 0.22 (0.07 to 0.66). Cochrane review (2026 update), 11 trials, 4,462 people: 2-hour vs 4-hour turning intervals—unclear difference (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.39, very low certainty); other interval comparisons equally uncertain. Trial of 1,226 ICU patients: wearable sensors with real-time alerts helped enforce 2-hour turns; pressure-ulcer incidence below usual care (RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.75, moderate certainty). Trial of 116 patients: prone (face-down) positioning had higher pressure-ulcer incidence than supine (face-up) (RR 4.55, 95% CI 2.31 to 8.98).
17-8.note: Grade B for three reasons. (1) The two mortality studies only show worse outcomes among people who already had ulcers—not proof that preventing ulcers lowers mortality. (2) Randomized trials on turn intervals are weak. (3) Mattress evidence is stronger but compared hospital mattresses—extrapolation to home mattresses. Daily sacrum/heel/hip/shoulder checks for non-blanching red are standard nursing practice without a dedicated citation. Care services long-term care insurance may cover: this section entry 7. Sudden leg swelling: treat as deep vein thrombosis, Section 13 entry 11. Long bed rest after falls or major injury: Section 1 entry 34.

17-9.t: If cataracts already affect walking, get an ophthalmology workup for surgery; if both eyes are affected, do not delay the second eye too long
17-9.cost: Accompany the elder to ophthalmology once; the doctor decides whether to operate. One eye per surgery; many hospitals do day surgery and discharge the same day. If both eyes have cataracts, operate in two separate procedures. Out-of-pocket cost depends on intraocular lens (IOL) choice and local basic medical insurance (医保) reimbursement—ask before surgery.
17-9.human: In women aged 70+, having first-eye cataract surgery sooner cut falls over the next year by about 34%; fewer people fractured bones. The number who fell at least once did not drop. Second-eye surgery showed no clear fall difference. Operated patients had about 16% lower hip fracture over one year.
17-9.gain: Randomized trial of 306 women aged 70+ with cataracts. Half had first-eye surgery within about 4 weeks; half waited 12 months per usual care. Over one year, early surgery cut fall counts by about 34%. Rate ratio 0.66, 95% CI 0.45 to 0.96. At least one fall: surgery group 49%, wait group 45%—no reduction. Two or more falls: surgery 18%, wait 25%. Fractures: surgery group 4 (3%), wait group 12 (8%). Cochrane included this trial: first-eye surgery in women reduced fall counts; second-eye surgery did not. Second-eye randomized trial, 239 women aged 70+: surgery group fall rate 32% lower but difference may be chance (rate ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.39 to 1.19). U.S. Medicare 5% sample: 1,113,640 cataract patients aged 65+ (2002–2009), observational only. Surgery associated with about 16% lower one-year hip fracture odds (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.81 to 0.87). Absolute difference 0.20 percentage points—about 2 fewer cases per 1,000 people.
17-9.note: Controversy: pooled across two randomized trials, the number who fell at least once did not fall significantly (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.55 to 1.17). Western Australia all-population hospital records: in the year after first-eye surgery, fall-injury admissions rose 27%; between the two surgeries such admissions were 2.14× the pre-surgery rate. Before–after designs cannot separate surgery from aging. Another Australian cohort found fall counts dropped most after second-eye surgery—so if both eyes have cataracts, do not delay the second eye too long. Between the two surgeries, be extra careful walking and on stairs. Cochrane also included a vision-intervention trial where fall counts rose about 57%. Surgery fixes clarity; fewer falls still need Section 1 entry 13 (balance and leg strength). Whether bones survive a fall: Section 1 entry 39 (bone density testing) and entry 40 (treat osteoporosis if found). National eye health planning states cataract restoration surgery is widely available at county level—not only big-city hospitals. Main beneficiaries: your parents and grandparents.

17-10.t: When an elder walks the dog, hold the leash in the palm—not wrapped on the hand—keep it short, and train the dog not to lunge forward
17-10.cost: Holding and shortening the leash costs nothing; walk with the elder once and show them. Training the dog not to lunge takes time; self-training or a dog trainer—trainers cost money and prices vary widely by region. Hard because elders often use retractable leashes and wrap the leash around the wrist—they must change the habit.
17-10.human: In the U.S., fractures while walking a leashed dog among people aged 65+ rose from about 1,700 to about 4,400 per year; about eight in ten were women. Hip was the most common fracture site; nearly three in ten needed hospital admission. About three-quarters of hand injuries from dog leashes came from the leash wrapped on the hand and the dog pulling. So hold the leash in the palm, keep it short, and train the dog not to lunge.
17-10.gain: U.S. emergency surveillance extrapolated nationally: leashed-dog walking fractures among people aged 65+, about 1,671 in 2004 and about 4,396 in 2017, a statistically significant rise. Among fracture patients 78.6% were female, 28.7% hospitalized. By single site, hip most common at 17.3%; by region, upper limb most at 52.1%. Another national emergency dataset (2001–2018): dog-leash-related injuries extrapolated to about 360,000 (exact 356,746). Of these, 193,483 were dog-pull injuries and 136,767 trips or entanglement. Injuries per million population rose from 25.4 to 105.5. One hand-surgery clinic over 5 years: 443 dog-leash hand injuries; about three-quarters were hand or finger entanglement with a pull (abstract: 337, 75.9%). About one-fifth needed surgery (96, 21.6%). U.S. CDC: 2001–2006, about 86,629 fall injuries per year associated with cats and dogs, 88.0% with dogs. Among dog-related falls, 26% happened while walking the dog and 21.2% from the dog knocking or pulling the person down.
17-10.note: Palm grip and not wrapping the leash are advice from that hand-surgery clinic. They state this protects fingers and wrist but not being pulled down when the dog surges. They also recommend a short leash: short leash limits the dog’s run-up and softens the pull; long leash snags and trips. A fully extended retractable leash is a long leash. No study compared retractable vs fixed leashes for fall risk; a 2024 review notes no data on leash type at injury. Training the dog not to lunge is mentioned by CDC and the fracture paper authors. The fracture paper also suggests smaller dogs for elders considering getting a dog. No study quantified how much these steps reduce falls—benefit magnitude judged small. Bone resilience: Section 1 entries 39 and 40. Balance practice: Section 1 entry 13. Whether dog walking counts as exercise: Section 2 entry 44. Main beneficiaries: your parents and grandparents.

18-1.t: Start by claiming what you’re entitled to: the national dibao program gives 3,600 yuan per child per year until the child turns 3
18-1.cost: Zero out-of-pocket expense. Simply apply at the local hukou office where your child is registered — one visit is all it takes.
18-1.human: If your child was born after January 1, 2025, and is under 3 years old, you qualify for this payment. One parent or legal guardian can submit the application at the child’s hukou office. The allowance is 3,600 yuan per year per child, paid out until the child reaches age 3. No personal income tax applies to this money, and it does not count toward any dibao or similar assistance calculations.
18-1.gain: As stipulated in the policy issued by the General Offices of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council, infants and toddlers born after January 1, 2025, and under 3 years of age are eligible for a yearly payment of 3,600 yuan per child. This amount is exempt from personal income tax and is excluded from calculations of household or individual income when determining eligibility for dibao or similar programs.
18-1.note: This is a nationwide baseline benefit. Certain provinces and municipalities also offer their own local subsidies, which can be claimed alongside this national payment. Over three years, the total comes to 10,800 yuan — a modest contribution toward raising a child. Do not let this amount influence your decision about whether or not to have a child.

18-2.t: Maternity leave lasts 98 days; maternity benefits are paid by the maternity insurance fund based on the employer’s average monthly wage from the prior year
18-2.cost: There is no cost to you. Your employer handles all the paperwork — you don’t need to do anything.
18-2.human: You’re entitled to at least 98 days of maternity leave, including up to 15 days you can take before the birth. If the delivery is difficult, you get an extra 15 days. For each additional child born, you receive another 15 days of leave. The money paid during this time is called maternity benefits and comes from the maternity insurance fund. If your employer hasn’t enrolled in this insurance, they must pay the benefits themselves.
18-2.gain: The length of maternity leave is set by the State Council: “Female employees are entitled to 98 days of maternity leave, including 15 days before delivery; an extra 15 days are added for difficult deliveries; for each additional child born, an additional 15 days of leave are granted.” The payments received during this period are known as maternity benefits. For employees covered by maternity insurance, these benefits are paid by the insurance fund at the rate of the employer’s average monthly wage from the prior year. Employees not covered by insurance receive benefits from their employer at the same wage level they earned before taking leave.
18-2.note: 98 days is the minimum standard mandated by the state. Most provincial regulations on family planning add at least 60 days of additional “reward leave” for childbirth, bringing the total to at least 158 days in most regions. The party responsible for paying wages during this reward leave varies by province.

18-3.t: Important to know: Employers cannot cut pay or fire workers due to pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding
18-3.human: During pregnancy, after giving birth, or while breastfeeding, it is illegal for employers to cut your pay or fire you. Violators face fines ranging from 1,000 to 5,000 yuan per employee. For infants under one year old, you are entitled to one hour of breastfeeding time each day, and employers cannot assign you overtime or night shifts. Instructions on how to file a claim can be found in Section 19.
18-3.gain: As stipulated by the State Council, “Employers must not reduce the wages of female employees, fire them, or terminate their labor or employment contracts due to pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding.” In other words, during these periods, employers cannot lower your pay, fire you, or end your contract. Mothers of infants under one year old are entitled to one hour of breastfeeding time daily, and employers must not require them to work extra hours or night shifts. Any violations result in fines of at least 1,000 yuan and up to 5,000 yuan per employee.
18-3.note: If you are illegally fired, refer to Section 19 for steps on filing a claim. Key evidence includes any written notices or messages regarding job reassignment or pay cuts — be sure to keep these records safe.

18-4.t: The time-cost calculation of raising kids is based on “whose time is being used,” not on “how hard it is”
18-4.cost: There’s no monetary expense — only time is spent. For children under 3, that time is essentially taken up around the clock. The difficulty lies in the fact that this happens daily, not just for a few tough days.
18-4.human: Count up all the hours spent caring for the child each day, plus every nighttime wake-up call. Then multiply that total by the hourly wage of the person doing the work. The resulting figure is usually far higher than the cost of formula and diapers. That’s why it’s best to discuss how responsibilities will be divided before having a child.
18-4.gain: By converting daily childcare time and nighttime interruptions into hours, then multiplying by the caregiver’s hourly wage, you arrive at a number that typically exceeds the cost of formula and diapers. Even unpaid tasks like childcare, cooking, and nightly wake-ups should be treated the same way — converted to hours and multiplied by a wage figure to be included in the total cost. The calculation method mirrors that used in Section 10 for household chores. Having a clear division of labor agreed upon beforehand makes it easier to decide whether to have a child.
18-4.note: The goal isn’t to produce a perfectly accurate figure. Rather, it’s to ensure both partners discuss responsibilities using the same calculation framework prior to having a child, rather than arguing about it afterward.

18-5.t: Breaking down costs into three periods: ages 0–3, compulsory education, and post‑compulsory education
18-5.cost: There’s no single fixed figure for total expenses; they vary widely depending on the city and the approach families take. The real challenge is to carefully separate the costs into these three periods instead of guessing a rough total.
18-5.human: For ages 0–3, most spending goes toward childcare arrangements — whether parents care for the child themselves, grandparents help out, or a professional is hired. During primary and middle school, the main expenses are housing and extracurricular activities. After that, costs center on further education pathways. Since spending patterns differ so much in each phase, lumping them together yields only an intimidating overall figure.
18-5.gain: The bulk of expenses in the 0–3 age range relate to childcare methods; for compulsory education, housing and after‑school programs dominate; later on, costs shift toward higher‑level schooling. Because these categories are distinct, mixing them obscures the true financial picture.
18-5.note: First, factor in any guaranteed financial support such as parental subsidies, maternity allowances, and yibao reimbursements; then determine what additional funds are still needed. Avoid basing decisions on widely circulated online estimates like “it costs X million to raise a child,” as their calculation methods are unclear and may omit or overstate certain items.

18-6.t: Keep separate accounts for having kids for your elders, for marriage, and for old-age security
18-6.cost: There’s no monetary cost — only the cost of having a sincere conversation. The real challenge is speaking openly about these topics without dodging them.
18-6.human: Others may expect you to have children, and that can certainly be one factor to consider. Yet the time and money involved are expenses you personally bear. “Relying on kids for old-age support” deserves its own separate calculation, since it hinges on another person’s financial capacity and willingness two decades down the line. Be sure to also write down the consequences of choosing not to have kids, so you can compare both sides fairly.
18-6.gain: The reasoning here mirrors that in Section 10. External expectations are valid considerations, but their associated costs must be recorded on your own ledger, not someone else’s. This is especially true for “relying on kids for old-age support,” which depends entirely on another individual’s future financial situation and willingness to help.
18-6.note: Make sure to list both the consequences of having kids and those of not having them, then compare them side by side. Recording only one side of the equation doesn’t truly qualify as keeping accounts at all.

19-1.t: Overtime pay runs at 1.5×, 2×, and 3×; if unpaid, complain to labor inspection, and late payment triggers an extra 50% to 100%
19-1.cost: No cost. Routinely keep copies of clock-in records, shift schedules, and overtime approval forms, and screenshot work-group messages where managers assign extra work. The hard part is remembering to save them every month.
19-1.human: Weekday overtime is paid at 1.5 times your wage. Rest-day overtime without compensatory time off is paid at 2 times. Work on statutory public holidays such as New Year's Day, Spring Festival, Labor Day, and National Day is paid at 3 times, and compensatory time off cannot substitute for that pay. If the employer refuses, file a complaint with labor inspection. After a payment deadline is set and the employer still does not pay, the employer must also pay an additional half to the full amount owed on top of the arrears.
19-1.gain: Normal working hours under the law are no more than 8 hours per day and no more than 44 hours per week on average. Weekday overtime is generally capped at 1 hour per day. Where special reasons require more, it must not exceed 3 hours per day, and the total in one month must not exceed 36 hours. Overtime pay has three tiers. Extending working hours on ordinary days: at least 150% of wages. Working on a rest day when compensatory rest cannot be arranged: at least 200%. Working on a statutory public holiday: at least 300%. For statutory public holidays, the law does not offer a “substitute with compensatory rest” option. If the employer arranges overtime but does not pay overtime wages, the labor administration department orders it to pay within a set period. If it still does not pay after that period, it must pay the worker an additional sum of 50% to 100% of the amount due on top of the arrears (nationwide).
19-1.note: Rest days and statutory public holidays are calculated separately. Statutory public holidays are only the legally designated days each year, such as New Year's Day, Spring Festival, Labor Day, and National Day. Long breaks created by moving rest days to bridge holidays count as rest days and are paid at 200%. “Company policy requires overtime approval” and “I stayed voluntarily” do not mean the employer may withhold pay, but they make evidence harder, so keep assignment and approval records. If the employer wants a comprehensive working-hours system or a flexible working-hours system, it must obtain approval from the labor administration department first; it cannot decide on its own. For dispute time limits for arbitration, see Section 8, Item 19.

19-2.t: Annual leave is 5, 10, or 15 days by cumulative service years; unused days are paid at 300% of daily wage
19-2.cost: No cost. Add up years worked at all employers once; social insurance payment records are proof. The hard part is refusing to sign a “voluntary waiver of annual leave” form if the company pushes one.
19-2.human: With cumulative service of at least 1 year but less than 10 years across all employers, you get 5 days of annual leave per year. At 10 years it is 10 days; at 20 years, 15 days. Job changes still count toward the total. If the employer cannot schedule leave and you agree not to take it, those days are paid at 3 times daily wage. Sign a “voluntary waiver of annual leave” form and you only get normal wages.
19-2.gain: After 12 consecutive months of work you are entitled to annual leave. The number of days follows cumulative working time—years at all employers added together. At least 1 year but less than 10 years: 5 days; at least 10 years but less than 20 years: 10 days; 20 years or more: 15 days. Statutory public holidays and rest days do not count toward annual leave days. Where the employer truly cannot arrange leave because of work needs and you agree in writing not to take it, it must “pay annual leave wages at 300% of the employee’s daily wage income” for the days not taken. That 300% already includes the normal wage for the day you would have worked, so the extra cash in hand is 200%. Daily wage = your monthly wage ÷ 21.75. Monthly wage is the average over the 12 months before payment, excluding overtime pay. If you joined the employer mid-year, days are prorated by remaining calendar days at that employer. On resignation, accrue and settle for the portion of the year already worked; excess leave already taken is not clawed back. If the employer neither arranges leave nor pays, it is ordered to correct within a deadline. If it still does not after the deadline, besides the annual leave wage payment, it must pay an additional sum equal to that amount as compensation (nationwide; effective 1 January 2008).
19-2.note: Cumulative working time must be summed across employers; if you changed jobs, do not count only tenure at the current employer. Only when the employee “does not take leave for personal reasons and states so in writing” may the employer pay only normal wages, so do not sign a “voluntary waiver of annual leave” form. If personal leave totals more than 20 days in a year and the employer does not deduct wages, you get no annual leave that year. Excessive sick leave also disqualifies you: less than 10 years of service—2 months; 10 to 20 years—3 months; more than 20 years—4 months. Home leave, marriage and bereavement leave, maternity leave, and work-injury wage continuation periods do not count toward annual leave.

19-3.t: Probation has a legal cap, wages must be at least 80%, and it can only be agreed once
19-3.cost: No cost. Before signing, spend a few minutes checking the contract term against the probation length.
19-3.human: For a contract of less than 1 year, probation is at most 1 month. For 1 to 3 years, at most 2 months. For 3 years or more, at most 6 months. The same employer may only put you on probation once; a second probation after transfer after regularization is unlawful. Probation wages must not be below the lowest grade for the same post or 80% of the contract wage, and must not be below the local minimum wage.
19-3.gain: For a contract of more than 3 months but less than 1 year, probation must not exceed 1 month. For more than 1 year but less than 3 years, not more than 2 months. For 3 years or more, and for open-ended contracts with no end date, not more than 6 months. For a contract for a defined piece of work, or a contract of less than 3 months in total, probation may not be agreed. “The same employer and the same employee may agree on probation only once”—one probation round per person at that company. If the contract lists only a probation period, that probation is void and the period counts as the labor contract term. Probation wages “must not be lower than 80% of the lowest grade wage for the same post at the employer or 80% of the wage agreed in the labor contract, and must not be lower than the minimum wage standard at the employer’s location.” If probation exceeds the legal limit and you actually worked, the employer must pay compensation for the excess period at the monthly wage standard after probation ends. During probation the employer may terminate only for the legally listed grounds and must explain the reason to the worker (nationwide).
19-3.note: Three common violations: a 1-year contract with 3 months of probation; a second probation after transfer following regularization; and “no social insurance during probation”—social insurance obligations start from day one of work regardless of probation; employer duties are in Section 12, Item 16. Being dismissed in probation does not mean zero pay; it depends on whether the employer’s stated reason is one of the lawful grounds for termination. Unlawful termination is compensated at 2N per Item 6.

19-4.t: If you are laid off, calculate N first: one month’s wage per full year, half a month if under six months
19-4.cost: No cost. Run the numbers once with a calculator; about ten minutes.
19-4.human: When you are laid off, statutory economic compensation is calculated like this: one month’s wage for each full year worked; at least six months but less than a year counts as a year; less than six months gets half a month. Monthly wage here is the average over the 12 months before you leave, including bonuses, allowances, and subsidies. If wages exceed three times the local average monthly wage for the prior year, pay is capped at three times that average, and years of service count for at most 12 years.
19-4.gain: Statutory economic compensation under the Labor Contract Law is what the employer owes when you are laid off—commonly called N. The formula: “one month’s wage for each full year of service … six months or more but less than one year counts as one year; less than six months, half a month’s wage to the worker.” If monthly wage exceeds three times the local average monthly wage of employees for the prior year, use triple that average as the cap, and count at most twelve years of service.
19-4.note: Monthly wage means average wage over the twelve months before the labor contract is terminated. Bonuses, allowances, and subsidies all count—not base pay alone. That is what employers most often understate. Whether this sum is subject to personal income tax is in Item 18 of this section (tax on compensation).

19-5.t: If the employer dismisses you without 30 days’ prior notice, it must pay one extra month’s wage
19-5.human: If the employer terminates you under the grounds where it must give notice—because you cannot work after illness or injury, cannot perform after training or reassignment, or objective circumstances changed—and it did not give 30 days’ written notice, it must pay one month’s wage on top of N. That is the common N+1. In negotiation, list that month separately; do not let the employer fold it into N.
19-5.gain: The Labor Contract Law gives employers two options when terminating under this article. One is “notify the worker in writing thirty days in advance.” The other is “may terminate the labor contract after paying the worker one additional month’s wage.” If they want you out immediately, they pay an extra month. That extra month is commonly called payment in lieu of notice (代通知金), counted separately from N. That month is based on your prior month’s wage; N uses average wage over the 12 months before termination—the bases differ.
19-5.note: The extra month appears only in the three situations under Article 40 of the Labor Contract Law: illness or non-work injury and, after the medical period, inability to do the original or reassigned work; inability to perform after training or reassignment; major change in objective circumstances at signing and failed negotiation. Other situations have no extra month: economic layoffs (Article 41) require only 30 days’ notice to the union or all employees; mutual termination proposed by the employer is N; serious misconduct termination by the employer has no compensation; unlawful termination is 2N. For the Article 40 three cases, keep N and the extra month separate in negotiation; do not let the employer count the extra month as part of N.

19-6.t: For unlawful termination, damages are double the economic compensation standard
19-6.cost: No cost. Arbitration takes several months. The hard part is staying with the process the whole time and not dropping out midway.
19-6.human: If termination is unlawful, damages are double the economic compensation standard—commonly called 2N. Whether termination is unlawful depends on the facts. Ask legal aid or a lawyer first, then decide whether to negotiate or go to arbitration.
19-6.gain: The Labor Contract Law provides that where an employer unlawfully terminates or ends a labor contract, it “shall pay damages to the worker at twice the economic compensation standard under Article 47 of this Law.” The calculation is to compute one economic compensation amount under that standard, then pay double.
19-6.note: This is the common 2N. What counts as unlawful termination depends on the facts. Consult legal aid or a lawyer first, then choose negotiation or arbitration; routes are in Section 7.

19-7.t: Do not sign “resignation for personal reasons”—once signed, N usually disappears
19-7.cost: No cost. The hard part is resisting pressure to sign on the spot.
19-7.human: Signing that you resigned for personal reasons usually wipes out both economic compensation and unemployment insurance. Voluntary resignation is not among the situations that trigger compensation, except when you leave because of employer faults such as unpaid wages or failure to pay social insurance. You do not have to sign the same day; sleep on it.
19-7.gain: The Labor Contract Law limits economic compensation to the legally listed situations. A worker who initiates departure is not included unless the reason is statutory employer fault such as unpaid wages or failure to pay social insurance. Signing “voluntary resignation” usually voids both economic compensation and unemployment insurance.
19-7.note: A common employer line is “sign first to process exit; compensation comes separately.” If they mean it, put it in the agreement on the spot; otherwise do not sign. Not signing that day has no legal downside; sleep on it.

19-8.t: Before leaving, save pay slips, attendance records, the labor contract, social insurance records, and chat logs
19-8.cost: No cost. About half an hour to archive materials. The hard part is remembering before you walk out.
19-8.human: In dismissal or wage-deduction disputes the employer must prove its case, but for overtime you must prove first, and employers only have to keep wage records for two years. Once you hand back the computer and accounts, you cannot get these materials back. With pay slips, attendance, social insurance records, and original chat logs in hand, you have something to use when the employer denies liability.
19-8.gain: Once you return the computer and accounts, these materials are gone for good. Labor disputes follow “who asserts must prove”: what you claim, you must prove. Where evidence is in the employer’s hands, the employer must produce it; failure to do so carries adverse consequences for the employer. In arbitration, if you cannot obtain employer-held materials, the tribunal may order the employer to submit them within a set time. For dismissal, termination, contract cancellation, wage reduction, and calculation of length of service, the employer bears the burden of proof. Overtime is different: you must first prove you worked overtime. If you show overtime records are with the employer and it will not produce them, adverse consequences shift to the employer. The employer is only required to keep wage payment records for at least two years. When paying wages, the employer must give you a personal wage breakdown. Without a written contract, the following can prove an employment relationship: wage payment records, social insurance payment records, work ID, employment registration forms, attendance records, and testimony of other employees. Chat logs count as electronic data and can be evidence. Submit originals; printouts from original records still count as originals. In one Shanghai procuratorate case, a worker sought ten years of minimum-wage shortfalls. First- and second-instance courts recognized only the last two years before resignation. The courts held the employer need keep only two years of records, so the worker had to prove the prior eight years. He had ten years of pay slips and bank statements, but the employer disputed authenticity of the slips. In August 2024 he applied for procuratorial supervision. After the procuratorate protested, the employer paid 19,000 yuan in a mediated settlement. He sued when the company cleared staff in 2021; by the supervision application about three years had passed (nationwide).
19-8.note: Save only your own employment-related materials. Do not take company source code, client lists, or technical documents—risks of taking them are in Section 11. For chat logs, do not rely on screenshots alone; keep originals on the phone and do not delete. Best to save pay slips and bank statements every month; if you sue years after leaving, the employer is not required to keep records from more than two years ago. That Shanghai case turned around because of a procuratorate protest; most people never reach that step. On exit, also obtain a termination certificate from the employer—see Item 17 of this section (termination certificate).

19-9.t: Before dusty, noisy, or chemical jobs, check the contract for hazards; the employer arranges and pays for three occupational health exams
19-9.cost: No cost. When signing, read the “occupational disease hazard disclosure” section line by line. Keep a copy of each exam report. The hard part is asking in person and getting the documents in hand.
19-9.human: When signing the contract, the employer must truthfully state in writing what occupational disease hazards the post has, how to protect yourself, and what benefits apply. If it concealed them, you may refuse that work and the employer cannot fire you for it. Three occupational health exams—before starting, while on the job, and before leaving—are arranged and paid by the employer. Without an exit exam, the employer cannot terminate the contract with you.
19-9.gain: The Law on Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases requires that when signing a labor contract, the employer explain four things: what occupational disease hazards the work may cause, what consequences may follow, how to protect yourself, and what benefits apply. The statutory wording is to “truthfully inform the worker and specify it in the labor contract; concealment or deception is forbidden.” If you are later assigned hazardous work not disclosed in the contract, the employer must inform you again truthfully and renegotiate contract terms with you. If the employer fails, “the worker has the right to refuse work involving occupational disease hazards, and the employer may not terminate the labor contract for that reason.” There are three exams: pre-placement, during employment, and pre-departure. “Occupational health examination costs shall be borne by the employer”; the employer pays and must inform you of results in writing. Without a pre-placement exam, the employer must not assign work involving occupational disease hazards. Workers with occupational contraindications must not be assigned prohibited tasks. If health damage related to the job is found, the worker must be transferred from the original post and properly placed. “An employer must not terminate or end the labor contract with a worker who has not undergone the pre-departure occupational health examination.” On leaving, you “have the right to obtain a copy of your occupational health surveillance file; the employer shall provide it truthfully and free of charge, and affix its seal on the copy provided.” That occupational health surveillance file must be copied truthfully, given free, and stamped on the copy (nationwide).
19-9.note: Three questions at interview roughly show whether the employer is serious: whether the post has occupational disease hazards, whether the contract states them, and who pays for the pre-placement exam. If they cannot answer or say “start first and we’ll see,” weigh the risk yourself. Exit exams are most often skipped: without a pre-departure exam, the employer cannot terminate or end the contract. That exam is also key material for a later occupational disease diagnosis; likewise get a stamped copy of the surveillance file before you go. Occupational disease itself follows the work-injury route; benefits start at Item 11 of this section.

19-10.t: Dust, noise, and chemical toxins cause irreversible harm: the employer must supply protective gear, and you can refuse work with no protections
19-10.cost: No monetary cost. The hard part is wearing particulate respirators, earplugs, and safety goggles consistently, and refusing unprotected tasks — coworkers may call you picky.
19-10.human: Pneumoconiosis, noise-induced deafness, and chemical eye burns are all statutory occupational diseases. Once lungs or hearing are damaged, they cannot be restored. You have the right to know what hazards the job carries and to demand protective facilities and personal protective equipment from the employer. You may refuse work without protections. Pay cuts or dismissal for using these rights do not count.
19-10.gain: The statutory list of occupational diseases, effective 1 August 2025, has 12 major categories and 135 conditions, including 4 open-ended clauses. The first category is occupational pneumoconiosis. It covers silicosis, coal workers' pneumoconiosis, graphite pneumoconiosis, carbon black pneumoconiosis, asbestosis, talc pneumoconiosis, cement pneumoconiosis, mica pneumoconiosis, potter's pneumoconiosis, aluminum pneumoconiosis, welder's pneumoconiosis, and foundry worker's pneumoconiosis, plus one open-ended clause. Occupational ear, nose, throat, and oral diseases include noise-induced deafness and blast-induced deafness. Occupational eye diseases include chemical eye burns and welder's flash keratitis. These injuries are irreversible; no treatment can restore lungs or hearing. The law gives four rights you can cite on the spot. First, to know what occupational hazards exist in the workplace, what harm they can cause, and what protective measures are required. Second, to demand qualified protective facilities and personal protective equipment and improved working conditions. Third, to criticize, report, and complain about violations of occupational disease prevention law and practices that endanger life and health. Fourth, «to refuse unlawful orders and forced work without occupational disease protections» — you may refuse noncompliant orders and unprotected tasks. And «any reduction of wages or benefits, or termination of the labor contract, because the worker lawfully exercised these rights is void». Pay cuts, benefit cuts, or dismissal for exercising these rights do not count (nationwide)
19-10.note: Choose the right mask: only particulate respirators block dust; gauze masks and disposable surgical masks do not. If the employer does not issue earplugs in noisy jobs, buy your own for a few yuan a pair — lost hearing cannot be restored. «Work two years, save money, and leave» does not hold for pneumoconiosis. Silicosis can appear years after you leave dusty work and can keep worsening. Off-duty health checks matter especially (see this section item 9 — three occupational health examinations arranged and paid by the employer). The revised catalog adds two categories. One is occupational musculoskeletal disease: carpal tunnel syndrome, limited to manufacturing workers who repeatedly use the wrists or apply force for long periods. The other is occupational mental and behavioral disorder: post-traumatic stress disorder, limited to police, health workers, fire and rescue, and other emergency responders in sudden-incident work. First aid for chemical splashes on the body: Section 13, item 21.

19-11.t: If you are injured at work or hit on the commute, apply for work-injury recognition first; if the employer will not file, file yourself
19-11.cost: No monetary cost — one trip to the social insurance administrative agency. Bring three items: a work-injury recognition application form, proof of employment, and a medical diagnosis certificate.
19-11.human: Injuries at work count as work injuries. Being hit on the way to or from work, when you are not mainly at fault, also counts. Without work-injury recognition, medical costs, wages paid while you heal, and disability benefits all vanish. The employer should file within 30 days. If it does not, you, your family, or the trade union can file with the social insurance agency within one year.
19-11.gain: Without work-injury recognition, medical costs, wages paid during the work-stoppage period for treatment (停工留薪期工资), and disability benefits all vanish. If the employer misses the 30-day filing deadline, it must pay all work-injury benefits due in that period itself
19-11.note: Treat the one-year limit seriously; do not delay. Time lost for reasons not your fault does not count toward that year: force majeure, restricted personal liberty, employer-caused delay, imperfect registration systems at the social insurance agency, or labor arbitration or litigation to confirm the employment relationship. If the employer stalls until the deadline passes, apply anyway and bring evidence of the delay. If the agency refuses to accept the application or you disagree with the decision, you may apply for administrative reconsideration or sue directly. If the employer denies work injury, it must prove its case. Keep your own records too: photos from the day, coworkers' contact details, medical records, and attendance. Article 16 of the regulations lists three exclusions: intentional crime, intoxication or drug use, and self-harm or suicide. Article 15 also lists «deemed work injuries»: sudden illness at work and at the workstation with death, or death within 48 hours after failed emergency treatment.

19-12.t: Do not trust «making it to your desk counts as work injury»: if you feel suddenly unwell, call 120 first, not the time clock
19-12.human: Rushing to the office when you feel unwell will not earn extra money. «Deemed work injury» requires sudden illness during working hours and at the workstation; illness on the way before you arrive does not qualify. Rescue beyond 48 hours also does not qualify. Minutes spent chasing those conditions cost you your chance to survive.
19-12.gain: «Deemed work injury» requires sudden illness «during working hours and at the workstation» with death, or death within 48 hours after failed emergency treatment. Delaying care to meet those conditions trades your chance to live for compensation you may never receive
19-12.note: Both conditions must hold: working hours and the workstation. Illness on the commute before arrival does not apply. If illness starts at the workstation and you are sent home or to hospital and die within 48 hours despite treatment, the rule may still apply. What matters is where you were when illness started, not where death occurs. Short videos that say «hold on until you reach the company and you get paid» get it backward. What changes outcomes is whether you reach hospital in the first tens of minutes after onset. The 48-hour line is fixed; treatment beyond 48 hours excludes the case.

19-13.t: If the employer did not enroll you in work-injury insurance, benefits still apply and the employer pays the full standard amount
19-13.cost: No monetary cost. If the employer disputes liability, arbitration or litigation can take several months from start to finish. The hard part is staying on top of the process for those months.
19-13.human: Even without work-injury insurance enrollment, work-injury benefits still apply. The employer must pay the same items and amounts in full. Non-enrollment adds penalties on the employer: order to pay premiums, a daily late fee of 0.05% from the due date, and a fine of 1 to 3 times the unpaid amount if still not paid. «The company has no insurance so it cannot pay» is false.
19-13.gain: The regulations state plainly: if an employer that should enroll in work-injury insurance did not, and an employee is injured, that employer pays benefits under the same items and standards as the regulations. Which payments and how much match enrolled cases; only the payer changes to the employer
19-13.note: «The company did not buy work-injury insurance for you, so it cannot compensate» is one of the most common lies in these cases. Non-enrollment only adds penalties on the employer; your benefits do not shrink.

19-14.t: After injuries stabilize, get a work-capacity assessment; disability grade maps directly to money
19-14.cost: No monetary cost. One work-capacity assessment process; expect waiting time before and after.
19-14.human: After injuries stabilize, a work-capacity assessment turns grade directly into money. The lump-sum disability benefit uses your own wage: grade 5 — 18 months, grade 6 — 16 months, grade 7 — 13 months, grade 8 — 11 months, grade 9 — 9 months, grade 10 — 7 months. Do not sign a «one-time settlement» agreement before the assessment result is out.
19-14.gain: The lump-sum disability benefit converts disability grade into months of your own wage, paid once. Grade 5 — 18 months, grade 6 — 16 months, grade 7 — 13 months of your wage. Grades 8 — 11 months, 9 — 9 months, 10 — 7 months of your wage
19-14.note: Grades 5 and 6 keep the employment relationship; you remain the employer's employee and receive a monthly disability allowance. For grades 7 through 10, when the contract ends or you terminate it, two more lump sums apply: a one-time work-injury medical subsidy from the fund and a one-time disability employment subsidy from the employer; amounts are set by the province. Do not sign a «one-time settlement» before the assessment result is out.

19-15.t: Three payments for work-related death: funeral allowance, dependents' pension, and one-time work-death benefit
19-15.cost: No monetary cost — one set of procedures.
19-15.human: Work-related death means three payments; do not negotiate on only one. Funeral allowance equals 6 months of the local prior-year average employee monthly wage. Dependents' pension is paid monthly from the deceased's wage: 40% to the spouse, 30% to each other dependent. The one-time work-death benefit is 20 times the prior year's national urban per capita disposable income — one figure nationwide.
19-15.gain: Work-related death money comes in three parts. First, funeral allowance: 6 months of the prior-year average employee monthly wage in the insurance pooling area. Second, dependents' pension from the deceased's wage, paid monthly: spouse 40% per month, other dependents 30% each per month. Third, one-time work-death benefit: 20 times the prior year's national urban per capita disposable income — one amount nationwide, not by region. For deaths in 2026, that payment is about 1.13 million yuan (113万元 / 1130040 元). The calculation is prior-year national urban per capita disposable income 56502 yuan × 20.
19-15.note: The one-time work-death benefit is uniform nationwide and updates each year with data from the National Bureau of Statistics. Reject «our local standard is lower» in settlement talks.

19-16.t: If you face long-term bullying, insults, or harassment at work, do not just endure it: record evidence, then complain, report, or arbitrate depending on what happened
19-16.cost: No monetary cost. Time to log dates, who was present, exact words, and to keep original chat screenshots and emails. Arbitration or litigation can take months. Changing jobs is the highest cost — whether to leave is your call.
19-16.human: People bullied at work later face roughly 60% higher risk of heart disease and stroke, and more bullying means higher risk. Years later, bullied workers are about twice as likely to have suicidal thoughts as others. Insults and mistreatment are not something you shrug off.
19-16.gain: For health: three Swedish and Danish cohorts together, 79,201 employed people aged 18 to 65. None had cardiovascular disease at baseline; mean follow-up 12.4 years. 9% reported workplace bullying in the past year. Bullied workers had about 59% higher risk of cardiovascular disease (coronary and cerebrovascular disease) (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.28–1.98). Those who faced workplace violence had about 25% higher risk (HR 1.25, 1.12–1.40). For both, more exposure meant higher risk. A Norwegian nationally sampled follow-up survey of 1,846 employed people, measured every two to three years for three rounds: bullied workers were about twice as likely to develop suicidal thoughts (OR 2.05, 95% CI 1.08–3.89). The reverse did not hold — prior suicidal thoughts did not predict later bullying. Legally, China has no dedicated «workplace bullying» statute; match the act to existing rules. Employers who insult, physically punish, beat, illegally search, or illegally detain workers face administrative penalties, must compensate harm, and bear criminal liability if applicable. If an employer uses violence or threats to force work, you may terminate the contract at once without prior notice and claim economic compensation. Employers must prevent and stop sexual harassment via authority or hierarchy; victims may hold harassers civilly liable. Labor arbitration closes within 45 days from acceptance; complex cases may extend up to 15 days more.
19-16.note: Graded B because health figures come from follow-up studies, not randomized trials, and «bullying» was self-reported. Four steps you can take now. Step one: start logging today; recording — Section 8, item 41. Step two: raise the issue in writing through internal channels and keep proof you did. Step three: if you are beaten, confined, or publicly humiliated, call the police. Step four: if unpaid wages or missing social insurance (社保) forced you out, follow this section item 7 (do not sign voluntary resignation) and item 8 (save evidence before leaving). How economic compensation is calculated: this section item 4 (calculate N when laid off). Pure cold-shoulder, exclusion, or petty obstruction often fit no specific statute; main routes are internal complaint, transfer, and changing jobs. Arbitration runs up to 60 days from acceptance; first-instance court is 6 months from the start; you pay your own lawyer. If you are at breaking point, call 12356 — Section 1, item 25. This item does not tell you to quit at the first insult; the cost of changing jobs is yours to weigh.

19-17.t: When you leave, get a separation certificate stating contract term, leave date, position, and years of service
19-17.cost: No monetary cost. Ask in person before you go, or send a written request and keep proof you asked. Hard when relations are bad. If the employer stalls, complaint or arbitration can take weeks to months.
19-17.human: Whether you were dismissed, the contract expired, or you resigned, the employer must give a separation certificate when you leave and transfer your personnel file and social insurance within 15 days. The certificate must state contract term, separation date, position, and years at this employer. You need it for unemployment registration. If the employer refuses, labor authorities order correction and must pay any loss they caused.
19-17.gain: The Labor Contract Law requires a certificate when the contract is terminated or ended. The rule does not depend on who initiated it — non-renewal, resignation, or dismissal all count. The employer must complete personnel file and social insurance transfer within 15 days. Implementing regulations require four items on the certificate: contract term, date of termination or end, job position, and years of service at the unit. The Unemployment Insurance Regulations require laid-off workers to take the employer's certificate promptly to the social insurance agency for unemployment registration. Unemployment benefits start from the registration date. If the employer does not issue a written certificate, the labor administration orders correction. If you suffer loss, the employer pays damages. The law also provides that a new employer who hires someone still bound to a former employer and causes loss to the former employer bears joint and several liability. The separation certificate is written proof that you and the former employer have ended the relationship (nationwide)
19-17.note: The law does not tie issuing the certificate to finishing handover; economic compensation is paid after handover is done. If the employer drags its feet, send one more written demand. If still no certificate, call 12333 or complain to labor inspection at the human resources bureau. Complaints are free; after a case is opened, investigation must finish within 60 working days, extendable 30 working days for complex cases. To claim damages from the employer, use labor arbitration — also free — within one year. After acceptance, arbitration closes within 45 days, extendable 15 days. You must prove the loss yourself, for example delayed unemployment registration or a new employer refusing you for lack of proof. If you disagree with the award, go to court; ordinary first-instance procedure starts at six months.
